{np}Go? Fool. Where would I go!{pp}No, the key is the boy. Kill him, and this ends!
{np}M'lord.
{np}The cur bites his master's hand, eh?
{np}Betrayer! Whose creature are you? Balbatos? Brantyn, maybe?{pp}Are you blind to the army at our gates? You place us all in jeopardy!
{np}I am no lord's creature! I seek only what the Resistance has always sought!{pp}Our ranks dwindle by the day! Can't you see it?{pp}The people no longer follow the duke!
{np}And so they follow you? Usurper! They say Heaven's justice is swift, but you deserve far swifter!

{np}Fool boy... I curse you...
With my dying breath, I curse you!
{np}We're going in, press the attack! Spare any who've lost the will to fight!

{np}Traitor to the Resistance! How quickly you forget your debt to the duke.{pp}Your kind are thorns in the heel of progress―how fortunate I bear the perfect remedy.{pp}My sword will teach you the right of things! Advance!
{np}You may have stopped me, but...our uprising will not die...so easily.

{np}Your Grace.
Sir Leonar has arrived!
{np}Leonar? Here? Perhaps there is yet hope.
{np}Your Grace, my humblest apologies for not coming sooner. Not hanging from the parapets yet, I see.
{np}No, good friend. But that rebellious upstart would be the first to see me so, no doubt.
{np}If he fails, the Bakram will have their chance soon enough. Rhime has fallen.
{np}Leonar!? But...why?

{np}Your Grace bears too great a burden.
Let me lighten your load.
{np}Listen well. I want no needless bloodshed. Make a path out of the castle, and drive out those who resist.
{np}Sir!
{np}Sir Leonar! What of the duke?
{np}All went according to plan, thanks to your effort.
{np}Then the duke is no more.

{np}Yes...
And all that remains is for you to join him!
{np}What!? What are you doing!?

{np}Something that would have been impossible were it not for you.{pp}You die, taking responsibility for both the revolt and the death of the duke, and the Resistance rallies to me.{pp}Truly, you have my undying gratitude, {hero}.
{np}You really think my death will accomplish so much?

{np}How could it not? Death is the ultimate absolution, and you have much to atone for.{pp}―Mostly {pal 16}my{palreset} sins, but no matter. You've played your role.{pp}Rest. Your days of sacrificing heart and soul to the Resistance are over.
{np}Venomed words―don't listen to him!{pp}It's as Vyce said. Leonar and the duke are the same: men, drunk on power!

{np}Respect, please!
I am twice the man he was.
{np}Rise, {hero}! This is not your place to die! I...I forbid it!

{np}I am sorry...
You will live on in my heart.

{np}Stand and fight, {hero}!
Have you forgotten your promise!
{np}You, Vyce? What are you doing here?{pp}Ah, I see. Old friends reunited. Very well. You can die together!
{np}Respect, please! I am twice the man he was.
{np}Now to restore the Resistance. Raise your sword, {hero}!
{np}I thought you different from all the rest, Leonar. But you love the nobility as much as they love themselves.
{np}If the nobility can provide a fairer rule, then they have my devotion.
{np}A fairer rule under the same despots? You dream if you think the nobles will serve as their own headsmen!

{np}You mistake me, Vyce. If a man wants power, he must claim it for himself. No noble will do that for him, true.{pp}Yet most commons wait for such a man, a savior to put things to rights. Whence this savior, then?{pp}Why not people like you―like me―the few who take up the sword to better their lot in life. They can be the next nobility, shepherds to the rest.{pp}And where the wrong in that? I know you desire change, but such is forged slowly, link by link, not made whole in the span of a night.
{np}You talk much of power, but what of honor?{pp}What possible claim to virtue could you make over {hero}'s disgraced corpse!

{np}I fear you lack sufficient dedication to understand. It is my dedication to a cause that trumps all such fleeting considerations.{pp}The man who wallows in sentiment accomplishes nothing. That is what it means to bloody your hands, boy!
{np}You forget whose blood it is!
{np}Vyce...thank you.
{np}Our paths crossed by chance. That's all.
{np}Be that as it may, I still thank you.
{np}Vyce, Arycelle...thank you.
{np}Fortunate for you that an even greater menace faces us both.{pp}I sheathe my hatred of you for the sake of the people, for now. Do not expect to find me so charitable next we meet.
{np}Leonar, put away your weapon! I do not wish to fight!

{np}Still clinging to some hope of reconciliation, you simpering waif? Know I will strike without hesitation!{pp}If you wish to live, if you wish to change this world on your own terms, then slay me!{pp}Fail, and only the worms will remember you.
{np}You leave me no choice!
{np}Gak... He's tough.
{np}Arycelle, withdraw!
{np}As you say.
{np}{hero}! I value my hide too much to throw it away here.{pp}It's up to you now. Live, so that Valeria will know what he's done.
{np}Brother...I come to join you.

{np}No, Arycelle!
She deserved a better death than this.

{np}It's over.
Well fought, {hero}.{pp}Go on, finish it.
Tell our people... Tell them this:{pp}It was my scheming brought us here.
{np}Did you intend this all along?

{np}Either death, yours or mine, serves to unite the Resistance.{pp}Though in truth, I had much rather it been yours. Ha.{pp}We harbor none of Vyce's nobles or their pets now, do we?{pp}The New Walister Alliance will...will join you. Welcome them.{pp}My eyes...grow dark.
My limbs numb.{pp}All rests on you now. You have the strength... You have the strength.
{np}The road to Coritanae is long. Why take her all that way?{pp}She's for the gallows at any rate. I say we have done with it here and now!
{np}Orders is orders. Commander Loxaerion is to have a proper hearing before her justice is meted out.
{np}And is it not some opposition nobleman who spares her?{pp}Why do you suppose they go to such lengths to keep her from harm?
{np}They say there's Galgastani blood in her. Might be that blood is bluer than most.
{np}Then her crime is twofold, for she is a kinslayer besides!{pp}I see no Galgastani before me―only a Walister knight!
{np}The Walister name me a Galgastani traitor, while the Galgastani claim I am a Walister knight.{pp}Enemy to all and friend to none.
{np}The Galgastani can't so much as escort a prisoner without a quarrel. No wonder the country splits in two.
{np}Silence her!
{np}I'll have a much easier time guarding you if you would guard your tongue.{pp}It'll mean my neck if I don't bring you back safe to Coritanae.
{np}Sir Alfred, it's the Walister!
{np}Now's my chance...

{np}What?
How!?
{np}Is that...Ravness?
{np}Damned woman!
{np}She's sealed her own fate. We've cause enough to kill her now.{pp}Kill kinslayer and rebels all!
{np}If you mean to seize me as a traitor, then do so. Else return to your duties.{pp}Tarry here too long and your master may wonder at your absence.

{np}{select 1}{FF 88 02}1{FF 88 02}.{FF 88 01} You are a friend, then?
2. I cannot leave you here.
{np}My lady, the Resistance hunts you, yet you act as a friend to us. Why?
{np}If you name "friend" only those who follow you blindly, then I am no friend of yours.
{np}A simple answer would have sufficed.
{np}The cards seldom give us simple answers, do they.{pp}But I will offer you this: so long as we share a common foe, I will not raise my sword against you.
{np}Wherever your loyalties lie, I cannot simply leave you to your fate.
{np}Not words I'd expect from a man with the blood of Balmamusa on his hands. But still only words.
{np}Believe me or not, as you will.
{np}He speaks plain enough. Perhaps the horrors of that day have wrought some change in him.{pp}I think I shall see for myself.

{np}If I fall now, all comes to nothing.{pp}I will not die here!
I must go on!

{np}Ravness!
They didn't hurt you, did they?{pp}When I heard the Galgastani had captured you, I feared the worst.
{np}Abuna Donnalto... You speak with such sincerity, I half believe you're worried.
{np}I deserved that. I've not forgotten the way we treated you at Balmamusa.{pp}But believe me, I want only to save you.
{np}To save me, you say? Well, I do believe you, actually.{pp}Only I wonder... What form this salvation?
{np}I do not think to mend the wound in your heart, but I can help save your life.{pp}And where there's life, there is always hope of salvation.
{np}I turned my back on my country... For what?
{np}Ravness, no!
{np}When a dog turns on its master, it must be put down!
{np}I let her die...{pp}She was no enemy, but a woman true and just. What have I done?
{np}Should have...killed her while I...had the chance.
{np}What do the Galgastani want with her...and she of them?
{np}I suppose I should thank you.{pp}Even if you lead me away a traitor, I owe you my life.
{np}Are you a traitor?
{np}She has Galgastani blood in her. Is it any wonder some tie remains?
{np}You speak as though she betrayed the Walister outright, Sister.

{np}Only words. Though no doubt there are others who share her thinking.{pp}Those who claim that, fearing for my life, I struck a deal with the Galgastani, who were only too willing to embrace one of their own.{pp}And there is some kernel of truth to it.{pp}I doubt even those Galgastani nobles who do not take so hard a line as Balbatos would have offered me shelter were it not for my blood.{pp}But in the final lay of the cards, I am a woman without a country.
{np}I'm sorry.
{np}I had always told myself I was a Walister, and I acted the part as best I could.{pp}But this... I am shaken to the core. I no longer know what I am meant to be.
{np}Ravness, come back with us. Warriors of your skill are in short supply. We could use you.
{np}I am cheered to hear you say so, but I...I can never go back.{pp}I cannot forgive the duke for what he did at Balmamusa...nor the disgrace I suffered there.
{np}I see.
{np}But my gratitude is heartfelt. Both for saving my life...and for setting me free.
{np}The duke wants her captured. Can we really just...let her go?
{np}Leave it be, Sister.

{np}You may find it hard to believe, but I love the Walister.{pp}I was born in Almorica―spent my childhood there. It will always be my home.{pp}Even now, I do only what I feel best for the Walister people.{pp}Farewell, {hero}. Perhaps we'll meet again someday.
{np}Are you certain this is the right choice? What if she joins forces with the Galgastani?{pp}Should you face her on the battlefield, it will not go easy for you.
{np}If she becomes an enemy for true, I will face her as any Walister soldier would.{pp}Do not worry, Sister. All will be well.
{np}Come, let's be off.

{np}What am I to do with you, Barbas? Hmm? One cannot deny your insubordination.{pp}To act without leave of the high champion is strictly forbidden, whatever the circumstance.{pp}Time and again you were ordered to return, and each time you've ignored your orders!{pp}Only now do you deign to grace these halls. I am galled.
{np}Galling, yes, the obstinate lout. Go on, beg forgiveness.
{np}You talk too much, Martym. And I have an ill temper.
{np}What was I to do? Deny the regent? Impossible.
{np}We do not answer to Brantyn!{pp}Speak true. You learned that the Xenobian knights were in Rhime and sought to do battle. Is it not so?

{np}Enough, Balxephon.
What's done is done.
{np}Welcome back, Lord Commander. I see Ozma and Oz accompany you.
{np}What word of the Walister?
{np}They rally their troops on Golborza, yet they do not make to march.
{np}I should think not. The duke has but a tenuous grasp on Galgastan.{pp}Dispatch an envoy. Explain our position to the duke and renew our vow to remain unaligned.
{np}And the Bakram? I cannot imagine the regent sits idle.

{np}Brantyn will be made hierophant, his age-old wish fulfilled. If that does not content him, nothing will.{pp}Controlling the isles is not our mandate. Nor can we afford the Xenobians to perceive elsewise.{pp}If we are to avoid giving them cause to intervene in Valeria, we must shun the sword in favor of the olive branch.{pp}So long as we are the advocates of peace, they dare not act. Is that clear, Barbas?
{np}...Aye.
{np}I'm sending you to Heim.
{np}But Heim is leagues from the front!

{np}Steady, Barbas. I do not intend for you to serve as castellan for the regent, if that is your fear.{pp}Abuna Prancet was being held in Heim Castle. Unfortunately, a band of rebels saw fit to free him.
{np}The work of the Liberation Front, no doubt. Regardless, I would prefer our true task remain secret.

{np}Mannaflora's whereabouts elude us, and now the abuna, the only man who might know, has gone missing as well.{pp}Barbas, I task you with a mission of utmost import. Recapture Abuna Prancet, whatever the cost.
{np}Yes, Lord Commander.
{np}The two of you are to deal with the Liberation Front. Too long have we suffered them to move unchecked.
{np}On the honor of House Glacius, my brother and I will see it so.

{np}Common rabble.
They'll be little trouble.
{np}Andoras's search for Mannaflora is to continue.{pp}You and Martym are to proceed with our negotiations with the duke.
{np}As my lord wishes, so shall it be.
{np}What part of the Galgastani have joined our cause?
{np}Half their men, perhaps a little more. Another third have deserted.
{np}Hmm. Then the rest are loyalists who will cleave to Balbatos unto the bitter end.
{np}Few as they are, they were the backbone of his army. The best of the best.{pp}Their support in the crofts and villages runs deep. They'll not fall easily.
{np}Who better to see that they do. Spare not a moment.
{np}It shall be done.
{np}The Bakram show no sign of moving farther south. There's solace in that.{pp}Perhaps some faint breath remains in our pact with the Dark Knights.{pp}Let us send another envoy and remove all doubt.
{np}And you, my Hero of Golyat, are to hunt down Vyce Bozeck, who fled behind the enemy's line scarce a month past.
{np}Must we avenge ourselves upon him?

{np}You do not understand the creature you hunt. Indeed, he must seem a strange species to you.{pp}You and I share common conviction, however different our methods and means.{pp}Else why would you have returned to my halls?{pp}Vyce is different. He fights not for convictions or ideals but out of some base bloodlust.{pp}Unguided by higher philosophy, he acts without thought.{pp}Judged by your measure, he is useless―and how that must enrage him!{pp}Now he thrusts this rage at you, his onetime friend, a hero to all the world.
{np}I had held out hope that Vyce might return this past month.{pp}But too much time has passed.{pp}Were we to wait any longer, we risk him becoming a grave threat to our Resistance.
{np}But to put a price on his head... Is that not going too far?

{np}It pains me, truly.
But it is the needful course, Catiua.
{np}Will you say nothing in his defense, {hero}?
{np}Do not look for Vyce to return. Not while I'm still here.
{np}As ever, my words fall on deaf ears.

{np}Fine.
Do as you like.
{np}Catiua!
{np}Let her go, {hero}.
{np}Then we are agreed?
{np}Ah, I'd nearly forgotten. Sir Mirdyn has returned.

{np}He has?
Were there any others?
{np}He and Warren. That's all.{pp}Warren suffered a grievous wound. No doubt a visit from you would do much to cheer him.
{np}The men stand ready, Sir Leonar.
{np}I'll join them with all haste.
{np}{hero}, let's away. I know this sits ill with you, but it is our duty.
{np}I make my offer one final time. Answer me, and your lives will be spared.{pp}Who leads your band of stragglers, and where is he? Your answer!
{np}You may take a Galgastani knight's freedom, Leonar, but never his pride.{pp}We do not sell friends, not even for the unkindest price. Would you do any different?
{np}I suppose I wouldn't. Very well.
{np}Then...

{np}Then we shall hold a public execution... However!{pp}In deference to your honor, we will not bind you, and will furthermore arm you as befits your former station.{pp}If you truly desire freedom, fight for it!
{np}Clansmen of Galgastan!{pp}Tell our wives and children of how we died here today, of our last service to our homeland!{pp}And tell them to avenge us!
{np}Words in the wind, soldier! Our ears are deaf to your cries.{pp}We know you who pledged fealty to Balbatos are the true blight upon this land.
{np}Glory...to Galgastan.
{np}Your leader's sword lies silent. Will you fight on?
{np}Then justice has been served. Those surviving will join our ranks from this day forth!{pp}We will show them that Walister do not scorn those who embrace our cause!
{np}Your leader's sword lies silent. I would ask that you sheathe yours.{pp}No more lives need be taken here today.

{np}Good. Then this brutal bloodshed ends now. The survivors will join our ranks, and we will treat them as brothers.{pp}Soldiers of Walister, understand that we must clasp hands, not swords, if we are to know peace.
{np}Canopus!

{np}And {hero}, too!
I am glad to see you both well.
{np}And you, Sir Mirdyn.
{np}How is he?
{np}The Star Seer remains lost in the mists of sleep. But he draws breath and is whole of body.
{np}That is well, then.{pp}And Lanselot and Gildas? Have they not returned?
{np}I've seen neither since the night of the Bakram attack.
{np}It was Sir Gildas who saved me from the Dark Knights' swords that night.
{np}Would that I had been warrior enough to return the favor...
{np}I am sure both will return unharmed. And besides, there was little you could do.{pp}...I hear you search for Vyce. You know where he makes his den?
{np}No, but there is a price on his head.{pp}Not many places where a wanted man can hide.
{np}He would have to go to ground―or well under it―to hide from both the Resistance and what remains of the Galgastani.

{np}Aye. As we were leaving Rhime, I received report that a company led by an unnamed Dark Knight had taken to the highroad.{pp}A commander he was, called to Heim to help defend the town from partisans.
{np}Of course. These partisans must be the Liberation Front.{pp}They intend to strike the fortress at Boed, I'm sure of it! If Vyce should be there...
{np}They'll have his head in a sack by the morn!
{np}We ought make for Heim at once, {hero}!
{np}How will you ride, Mirdyn?
{np}With your party, of course.{pp}{FF 92}{hero}, I know you serve His Grace, but I also know you would not leave Vyce to die an ignoble death.

{np}Good.
Let us ride.
{np}{FF 9A 03}You received a White Knight's Mark.
{np}Sir Mirdyn, it is good to see you well.{pp}Tell me, how fares Warren?
{np}That's some relief, then.{pp}And Lanselot and Gildas? Have they not returned?
{np}Then I must go at once!
{np}Wait. I will ride with you.
{np}I know you serve His Grace, but I also know you would not leave Vyce to die an ignoble death.
{np}Gave us quite a chase, Abuna, but now it's back to Heim for you.
{np}Godless woman. You...you killed them all!

{np}Our work is done, Oz.
We withdraw.

{np}Hold, Sister.
I've another prize: the leader of the rabble.
{np}Bring her forward!
{np}Slew every Bakram soldier that marched with us from Rhime, this one did. A real firebrand.{pp}But she doesn't hold a candle to you, dear sister.
{np}Kill me and have done with it!
{np}Cerya! You live!
{np}Forgive me, Abuna. This is not how I meant to meet again.
{np}You've no cause to seek forgiveness. It is I who have troubled you.
{np}If you see my father, tell him his daughter met an honorable death.
{np}Is this touching melodrama played out?
{np}Take him away.
{np}Think not on the grave, Cerya. Live. And know they dare not kill me.
{np}What do you plan to do with her, Oz?
{np}She'll make a fine gift for the high commander, I should think.
{np}Oh? I recall no order to take her alive.{pp}Besides, look at her.{pp}She'd sooner choke on her own tongue than go a willing captive.
{np}Her eyes give the truth to your words.{pp}What am I to do with her, Sister?
{np}You rely on me too much, little brother. Decide for yourself.
{np}Such bile. So be it. But where to begin?{pp}{FF 92}Darkest lords of Vuira Viou, grab fast these legs and drag them down!
{np}You've a wicked streak, Oz.{pp}Enjoy your games, but don't tarry too long.
{np}Run, if you can.{pp}Name your conspirators and the location of their fastness, and I'll spare your meager life.
{np}Damn! We're too late!
{np}Cerya! We're coming!
{np}Feh, I've drunk my fill of these Walister dregs. A Dark Knight's work is never done.

{np}Cerya!
My dear sister!
{np}A sister? I'll be sure you're close at hand to watch your sibling draw her last breath!
{np}Why have you come back, Cistina? Leave this place while you can!{pp}You walked away from the Liberation Front. This is not your battle!
{np}I've come to save you, you ungrateful fool!{pp}I cannot bear to lose my sister. And the Front cannot bear to lose its leader.
{np}Senseless blather. The Liberation Front is dead.{pp}We hacked its body to bits with our swords. Only the head, such as it is, remains.
{np}Front or no, while we draw breath, our deeds can yet change Valeria!

{np}Cerya!
Are you unharmed?
{np}More vermin come out of the woodwork? This place teems with you rabble!
{np}Why have you come back, Folcurt? Leave this place while you can!{pp}You walked away from the Liberation Front. This is not your battle!
{np}You might show a bit more gratitude to a man who's come to save your life.{pp}Regardless, you'll not be so easily rid of me. The Front is oathsworn to aid those in peril.
{np}So long as we have friends of like conviction, we will never fall to you!
{np}I never thought to see you captured by the likes of these scoundrels. You disappoint me, Cerya!
{np}You! Old man! You know this woman, do you?{pp}Ah, another of her rats, no doubt.
{np}Why have you come back, Bayin? Leave this place while you can!{pp}You walked away from the Liberation Front. This is not your battle!

{np}This is no time for posturing, Cerya. We've come to save you.{pp}What matter the difference in our banner or philosophy?{pp}Our ends are the same, if not our means. Did we not start this battle to save the lives of our kinsmen?

{np}Have you not eyes to see the warriors before you? You've killed nothing!{pp}Fell one group, and another will rise to take its place.{pp}If a lasting peace you seek, you will leave these isles and never return.

{np}Your father, {hero}.
He...lives.

{np}My father...?
What? How!?
{np}You must...rescue him from the Dark Knights. Your father knows... He knows.
{np}Cerya!
{np}Cerya, no!
{np}You're a formidable lot. Still rabble, yet perhaps not so common.
{np}Now that you know your enemy, you would do well to lay down your sword. To do otherwise is to throw yourself upon it.
{np}You dare threaten me, baseborn knave? How I hate these wretched isles and all who dwell upon them!{pp}You squabble over Valeria like beggars over scraps. The sooner she is rid of you, the better!
{np}Show him no quarter!
{np}If you had an inkling of all this world encompassed, you would know the piddling place you held in it.{pp}But you do not, and so are your isles forever mired in blood and death!
{np}You and your kind brought this war to our shores!
{np}No! You have summoned us here. We come to quiet the storm.{pp}We bring order where there is chaos―peace where there is war!
{np}Do all knights of Lodis mantle themselves in such twisted truths?

{np}The dwarf lectures the giant? Ha! You are more fool than I thought.{pp}Lodis is a land of kings! Think you we care about the scraps of some unruly rabble?{pp}What can you know, you who hasten toward your own destruction? Destroy yourselves as you like, but do not visit your ruin upon us!
{np}You there! Dark Knight! Do you always justify your own misdeeds by finding fault in others?
{np}The listless drawl of a Xenobian... You must be Canopus. We encountered your countrymen at Rhime.
{np}How...?
{np}Any truth to the rumors that you were driven from your homeland? Such a sad tale.{pp}What's this now? The color has fled your cheek.
{np}If you set out to anger me, job's done. I'll carve you like a roast!
{np}You would make a poor mummer, Canopus.{pp}I see you for what you truly are.
{np}Let's hear it then.

{np}Once, in a battle, you weighed duty against friendship...and friendship won. You renounced the sword that day.{pp}So why do you play these piteous islanders false?{pp}You act the plain-spoken man to divert them from Xenobia's true intent!
{np}A fair speech for so foul a tongue. Tell me, are all knights of Lodis so long-winded?{pp}Just as well for you to savor your last words, I suppose.
{np}Your kind ever were an ignoble lot. Pity my sister is not here. She would have pleasured in your death.
{np}It's a dark day sees the likes of you...get the better of me.
{np}Where is my father? Why did you take him from Golyat?
{np}So you're the...abuna's boy...
{np}It's a dark day sees the likes of this rabble...get the better of me.
{np}My friends may be lost, but my battle is not over.
{np}{hero}...your father, Abuna Prancet. He lives.{pp}We held him safe in our care until a short while ago.

{np}What? How...?
Where is he?
{np}The Dark Knights left with him just before you arrived.
{np}Why would they bestir themselves over one man?
{np}The Dark Knights care nothing for who rules the isles.
{np}{hero}, it is your father, Prancet Pavel, whom they seek.
{np}What could they possibly want with him?

{np}I know little more than you. But I can offer one piece of the puzzle.{pp}They seek someone―or something―called Mannaflora. Whatever it may be, they are bent on finding it.{pp}And there is but one man who knows where it is.
{np}My father.
{np}Your father holds the key to this war.
{np}Is it possible―was he the reason they attacked Golyat?
{np}You had best leave. There's no knowing when they might return.
{np}And what will you do, Sister?
{np}I...I mean to help Abuna Prancet.
{np}Alone? Foolishness! What can you hope to accomplish?
{np}She'll not listen to me. Perhaps you can dissuade her from this madness!
{np}Madness is a bit...well, yes. What if you were to come with us?
{np}I am sorry, but I will not serve under a duke who sanctions the slaughter of innocents.{pp}Besides, I have my own duties as head of the Liberation Front.{pp}I owe it to our fallen to carry on.
{np}Sister...
{np}Look after Cistina for me.
{np}Our father is alive... I must tell my sister!
{np}Why would the Dark Knights go to such lengths to capture one man? It's absurd.
{np}They care nothing for who rules the isles.{pp}It is your father, Prancet Pavel, that they seek.
{np}And what do you intend, Cerya?
{np}I...I plan to help your father.
{np}Alone? You can't be serious! What can one person hope to accomplish?{pp}Join us. You know it to be the wiser course.
{np}I understand.
{np}My thanks. I could ask no more.
{np}Father lives... I must tell Catiua!
{np}Then you're telling me we don't know where Bozeck has gone?
{np}That's right, my lord. Nor did the Dark Knights give any indication they knew.
{np}This business with the Dark Knights―why did you engage them?
{np}I...I don't understand, my lord.
{np}You knew full well that Galgastan had not yet been brought to heel.{pp}But still you slew a commander of the Dark Knights.
{np}We can ill afford to make an enemy of them now.{pp}You were tasked with finding the renegade Vyce Bozeck, were you not?{pp}Better to have left that rabble rouser to fend for herself!
{np}I...I couldn't...

{np}Enough.
What's done is done.
{np}Dispatch an envoy to Phidoch. There is yet time to settle this with ink and quill.
{np}Yes, my lord.
{np}Further, we will raise the price on Bozeck's head to 10,000 goth.

{np}We cannot suffer him to come and go as he wills.{pp}With a bounty so high, he will think twice before making his presence known.{pp}As for the rest, it is in the hands of the headhunters.{pp}Our foremost concern is rooting out what followers of Balbatos remain and securing Coritanae.
{np}To which end, I want you to travel to Asyton.
{np}To find these followers of Balbatos?

{np}Difficult to say. We know only that you face a formidable foe.{pp}We've not heard from one of our companies stationed in Asyton for some time now. We believe they are responsible.{pp}What's worse, the casualties were not limited to our soldiers. Many smallfolk have turned up dead as well.{pp}Our response must be swift, decisive. I wish for you to lead it. I trust I may rely upon you?
{np}...Yes, my lord.
{np}Splendid. You're to leave at once.{pp}Oh, there was one other thing. Scarce more than a rumor, in truth.
{np}We are told that a man matching the description of the Xenobian knight Sir Gildas has been seen in Asyton.

{np}Sir Gildas?
What would he be doing there?
{np}Took fright and fled from Rhime, no doubt. Bloody coward.
{np}Sir Gildas is no coward!

{np}Silence!
I'll not have you at each other's throats!
{np}Go to Asyton. Send back word of what has happened. I know our hero will not disappoint.
{np}Sister, wait!
{np}What does the great hero need of me?

{np}Please, don't.
You're still upset, aren't you.
{np}If you have no urgent need, I'll be on my way.
{np}It's Father. He's alive!
{np}What?

{np}So he lives.
What now?

{np}What now?
We rescue him! What else?
{np}Even if he is no true father to us?
{np}I mean we are orphans, Brother. He is not our father. Not by blood, at any rate.
{np}No... Who told you this? It's a lie! It must be!
{np}It is no lie. I overheard him talking about it once, long ago.{pp}In all the world, you're the only family I have.
{np}Why tell me this only now?
{np}Because you're leaving me.
{np}Leaving you? Scarce a moment goes by we are not at each other's side!{pp}And so it shall remain. I will never leave you.
{np}There is the lie!{pp}Someday, you will cast me aside as you did Vyce!
{np}No, Sister.
{np}I'm alone without you...
{np}I remember you, boy! The Wheel brought us back together, has it? Someone up there must like ol' Ganpp.{pp}Obda! Berda! To me!
{np}You're well acquainted with Berda and Obda, but I been brewin' something special for just such an occasion!{pp}Banga! Zanga! To battle!
{np}Time to repay His Eminence's kindness. Today you feed on the rich stew of vengeance!
{np}Obda! What have they done to you! Your sorrow is my strength!
{np}Berda! My sweet Berda! Your anger feeds my own!
{np}Forgive me, Banga! Your soul will live on in me!
{np}They'll pay dear for this, Zanga! My heart ain't so gentle as yours!
{np}Piss and blood! The day is theirs!
{np}Next we meet will be the last! I won't forget what it was you done here!
{np}The Balbatos loyals fell upon them at Tynemouth. A tenacious lot, I'll give them that.{pp}We lost near twenty men uprooting those who had gone to ground in the city.
{np}What business is it of his? Why are you here, Hero?{pp}Come to aid the hierophant's men as you did the partisan rats in Boed?
{np}Enough.
{np}But he is a traitor!
{np}I said enough!
{np}Forgive her, {hero}. She speaks in anger.
{np}Hmph.

{np}I hate to part so soon, but I fear I must.{pp}They've taken captives and holed themselves up in Qadriga Fortress.{pp}I douse one fire, only to have ten others kindle in its place. No rest for the weary, eh?
{np}Do not let her words dishearten you, {hero}. I know you for the man you truly are.
{np}Dievold, Brother!
{np}What's going on down there?
{np}Gildas! Wait!
{np}No, stay away!
{np}Stand back, Oelias!
{np}Help... Please, help us!
{np}We'll be there as soon as we can!

{np}Dievold, no!
No...how could this have happened?

{np}Oelias! No...
Great Father! What have I done!?

{np}The dead drag me...down.
Forgive me, Oelias.

{np}Now I see...
With my dying breath...I curse you, Nybeth!
{np}What has befallen Gildas?
{np}Thank you for your aid, knight. I am Oelias.
{np}And this is my brother. Forgive his silence. He is not given much to conversing.
{np}No, I would thank you myself.{pp}My name is Dievold... Forgive my rasp.
{np}My brother is...ill. It has ravaged his throat.
{np}I am {hero}. I fight for the Resistance.{pp}Please, you must tell me what has happened here.
{np}That knight who attacked―the one with the foreign crest upon his armor. He was one of yours?
{np}Gildas, you mean? Yes, he was a staunch ally.{pp}I had not seen him since the night of the Bakram attack on Rhime.{pp}No one knew what had befallen him.
{np}Ah...then I have ill news for you.{pp}That was not the man you know.
{np}No, I'm quite certain that was Gildas.
{np}You mistake me. Did you not see them? The ones pallid of flesh?

{np}What, the zombies?
...What are you saying?

{np}You don't mean that Gildas...
That he was― No!
{np}There is a man who wields the walking dead as you wield your sword.
{np}He plays with death, defiling the very substance of life and profaning all that is sacred.
{np}Who is he?
{np}The most vile necromancer in Galgastan, Nybeth Obdilord.{pp}...My father.
{np}I am Oelias Obdilord, the necromancer's daughter, though it gives me no pride to say it.
{np}Nybeth! What foul turn is this?
{np}Please, you must let us join your Resistance.{pp}We would aid you in defeating the necromancer.
{np}You'd fight your own father? For true?
{np}Yes. My brother...
{np}Your eyes will tell you what my tongue cannot.
{np}Ah!?
{np}What...are you? Do you even live!?
{np}Hmph. A riddle, to be sure, to which not even I know an answer.{pp}My bones are knit with magics, not sinew. What's more, though my head is mine, my body is another's.

{np}My brother...was executed by Balbatos when the warring began, as an example to others who would defy the hierophant.{pp}But my father, Nybeth, used a soul-fetching spell to call him back from the shores of death.
{np}A soul-fetch...?

{np}Yes. I was returned to this world against my will. A full five days after my departure.{pp}When I awoke, I found that my body was not my own. My father had affixed my head to another corpse.{pp}He told me then that my old body had suffered damage too great to be of further use.{pp}But...I suspect that was a lie. He merely wanted to see if the transposing would work.
{np}That, and the soul-fetch was incomplete.
{np}It is a difficult thing to fetch a departed soul and seat it within a mortal shell.{pp}Though my father's magic did bind me to this body, I know not how long it will endure.
{np}What happens when the spell wears off?
{np}Death. Again.
{np}...I'm sorry.

{np}Our father...continues his experimentations, trying to perfect the spell.{pp}He has even joined in league with Balbatos―the very man who killed his son―to satisfy his need for corpses.{pp}I... I hate him! I hate him for his betrayal, and for what he did to my brother!

{np}{select 1}{FF 88 02}1{FF 88 02}.{FF 88 01} Very well, you may join us.
2. I'm sorry, but I must refuse.
{np}Join our ranks. March with us.
{np}Thank you. You'll not regret it.
{np}Let us after Nybeth, then.{pp}I've seen enough of his dark work here. I do not care to see more.
{np}I have heard that our father has crossed the straits to the isle of Banhamuba.
{np}Then we must make haste.
{np}I do not see how you can aid us, ardent though you may be.
{np}You are right, of course. What use a sybil, untrained in combat? I should not have asked.{pp}Farewell, knight. Thank you for your help.
{np}If you would pursue our father, cross the straits to the isle of Banhamuba. Stop him, lest the dead never know rest.
{np}May the Light shine upon your path.

{np}Nybeth would give his very life to the darkness to sate his desire for knowledge.{pp}As for others' lives, he cares not one whit. Humans are as insects to him, subjects for experimentation.{pp}I saw it myself when my brother died. Why mourn, when my brother's passing provided the perfect opportunity to work his sorcery?
{np}I hate him... With all my being, I hate him!{pp}Now that my brother has finally been laid to rest, it is my father's turn!

{np}{select 1}{FF 88 02}1{FF 88 02}.{FF 88 01} Very well, you may join us.
2. I'm sorry, but I must refuse you.
{np}If you would pursue my father, cross the straits to the isle of Banhamuba. Stop him, lest the dead never know rest.
{np}I thank you for your help.{pp}My name is Dievold... Forgive my rasp.
{np}That knight who attacked Oelias―he with the foreign crest upon his armor. He was one of yours?
{np}Gildas, you mean? Yes, he was a staunch ally.{pp}I had not seen him since the night of the Bakram attack on Rhime.{pp}The woman who fell in the battle―Oelias, you said?―who was she?
{np}She was my blood...
{np}Then I am sorry we could not save her.
{np}When the warring began after Dorgalua's passing, I was executed―an example to others who would rise against Balbatos.
{np}Executed!? How―
{np}You know of the necromancer, Nybeth?
{np}Aye, though I wish I did not. The necromancer of Galgastan, Nybeth Obdilord, is a curse given flesh.
{np}Yes, he is a curse. And also my father.
{np}Your father!
{np}My father Nybeth used a soul-fetching spell to drag me back to the world of the living.

{np}As if that was not enough, the soul-fetch was incomplete.{pp}It is a difficult thing to fetch a departed soul and seat it within a mortal shell.{pp}Though my father's magic did bind me to this body, I know not how long it will endure.
{np}That outland knight you called your companion ran afoul of my father...
{np}No...
{np}I am sad to say that he and I are of a kind, now. No longer truly part of this world.
{np}No... Damn him!

{np}I would offer you my aid in exchange for yours. Nybeth must be stopped.{pp}To let him live would be to sow the seeds of some future strife.{pp}...And swell the ranks of his victims, like your friend, and Oelias...and myself.
{np}I thank you. What time remains to me shall be yours.
{np}The woman... Oelias, you called her? She, too, was a victim?
{np}That...is a tale for another day.
{np}Nybeth is out there. Let's be off.
{np}I understand he has crossed the straits to the isle of Banhamuba.
{np}Though I do not doubt your willingness, I do not think you can help us.
{np}I understand. Promise me, then, that you will use caution. Nybeth is mad, but no less dangerous for it. Perhaps more.
{np}If you would pursue him, cross the straits to the isle of Banhamuba. Stop him, lest the dead never know rest.
{np}You are far from home, {hero} of Golyat!

{np}{hero}, you say?
Then we are betrayed! Cursed Sister...

{np}Nothing I can't handle, Cressida.
Go now. Inform Master Nybeth of our visitor.
{np}What? And leave you here alone, Mother? You must permit me to stay, I beg you!
{np}Do not worry yourself over me. Master Nybeth's artifact will serve, should it come to that.{pp}Now, get you gone!
{np}Have care, Mother!

{np}Denizens of the abyss! From ink of blackest night, I summon you!
Darkness to me!
{np}The blood of my dearest daughter, Moldova, stains your hands. Blood calls for blood.
{np}I did not think to need this now...
{np}What!? No! Nybeth has doomed me!
{np}One false step near that pit, and they'll need no swords or sorcery to do us in.
{np}That you profane this temple can only mean my mother and I are forever parted.
{np}It is she who profaned the dead. I'll not mourn her passing. Yield now, or rejoin her in the Ever-World.
{np}Who are you to judge, you who have slain legions in your war?{pp}The wage of your ambition is paid in the lives of others. You can never understand the prize for which we struggle.
{np}You use souls and corpses for sport! No prize is worth such sacrilege.

{np}I've no time to argue with the likes of you. I must focus on the task at hand, both for my sister, and now my mother.{pp}Your corpse will make a fine gift for Master Nybeth!{pp}Denizens of the abyss! From ink of blackest night, I summon you!
Darkness to me!
{np}Master Nybeth...forgive me...

{np}Sir Gildas! Are you here?
Answer if you can hear me!
{np}Hrm... The flesh has already begun to fail. I have yet to perfect my art.
{np}A living-corpse incantation yields the subject undead.{pp}Resurrect restores life to the body, but does naught for the soul.
{np}But Dievold fared better than most.{pp}His memories remain intact. That's one hurdle cleared, at least.
{np}But what is the mind without the body?
{np}Each new success brings only another failure.{pp}But such are the restraints I must work against. No small task, restoring life to the dead.
{np}Another of my works, a failure. Forgive me.

{np}Clearly it is not enough to call the soul back to a house no longer fit to hold it.{pp}But what if there were some means of leaving behind the shattered body―a transmigration of the soul?{pp}Perhaps that way lies the path to vanquish death.
{np}If I must resort to the tools of the magi to learn the secrets I seek, then so be it.

{np}Ah, what's this?
A visitor?
{np}Please, Father, you must stop this! Put an end to this suffering!

{np}What suffering? You can't mean my zombies!{pp}They attack of their own will.{pp}They cannot abide the living, and death is an agony. They simply seek more of their own, and I have given them hope!{pp}It is gratitude I am owed, not resentment.{pp}Don't spout that tired doctrine the church passes for truth!{pp}You were too weak to save Dievold's soul. What makes you think you can save these others?
{np}I'll not turn my back on them and run as you did!{pp}I do not despair of life as you, Father. I revel in each moment!

{np}Ever the self-righteous one. A quality I found endearing, once.{pp}I will not enjoy killing you, but I see no other way.{pp}Denizens of the abyss! From ink of blackest night, I summon you!
Darkness to me!

{np}Sir Gildas!
It's me, {hero}!
{np}Do you remember him? He was a friend of the man you were.
{np}A friend...
{np}Think well. You saved his life at Rhime.
{np}Saved him...yes...
{np}That's right. You died at Rhime―died saving him.{pp}Had you not done so, you would be alive today, not he.{pp}You despise him! All you have suffered in death is because of him!
{np}I must...kill him.

{np}If that is your wish, I'll not deny you.{pp}Crush the life from his lungs! Visit death upon him!{pp}Denizens of the abyss! From ink of blackest night, I summon you!
Darkness to me!
{np}Sir Gildas!
{np}Suffering... Pain...

{np}No use talking to him. He is beyond the gift of thought.{pp}His flesh is failing now, though I scarce expect you to understand.{pp}I had such high hopes after his first few revivals. Alas, for him, there will be no escape from death.
{np}Is there no way to save him?
{np}He died at Rhime. There is no saving him now.{pp}For all my knowledge of the necromantic arts, I cannot change his fate.
{np}Gildas is lost, {hero}!{pp}All we can hope to do is free his soul from its rotting cage!
{np}He's quite right, you know. You must kill him if you wish to end his torment!
{np}You monster!
{np}I am sorry, Gildas. You will have peace soon!
{np}Nybeth...Father! You must end this! Your sorcery brings only suffering!

{np}How can you say such things, Dievold? Is it not thanks to my power that you stand here now?{pp}Yes, my techniques are imperfect. I will be the first to admit I have caused discomfort!{pp}But, when I do perfect them, then we will know true succor from the ravages of death! Is that not worth some pain along the path?
{np}What you do sins against life. It is a twisting of the Great Father's providence.{pp}It can never be perfect, for by its very nature it is corruption!

{np}Great Father? Don't chastise me with faerie tales, child. I am the only father you will ever have!{pp}You expect me to bend to the will of an imaginary being, when my own purpose lies so clearly before me?{pp}We are born only to die. If that is the providence given us by life, then I reject it!{pp}I make my own way through this world. My steely will, my shining intellect―these are light enough for me to follow!
{np}Then I must slay you before you take any more down your twisted path to hell, old man.
{np}Yes. Enough of words. Deeds bring transformation! Swing your sword as you will!

{np}I don't understand. What possible benefit could your abhorrent inquiries merit?{pp}I have no love for death, but I know better than to seek to change it, to bend the laws that bind us to our fate.{pp}Nor do I believe that life unfairly reclaimed is a true life. Lashing a tortured soul to a corpse is not salvation―it is cruelty!
{np}How my own flesh and blood cannot see the wonder I work is beyond me.{pp}Does the world not lament the veil of death, and likewise rejoice to see it lifted?
{np}You disregard death's purpose. It is the final reckoning toward which we strive.{pp}Life's ambrosia is sweet only when we know the cup will run dry!
{np}The same words you said to me before.{pp}Yet they still ring false, a paper-thin veneer that cannot disguise your fear. Death terrifies you, as it does us all.
{np}I fear death, yes, yet I will strive to accept it when my time comes.{pp}For I believe in my heart that death brings more than despair!
{np}What fell change has come upon me?
{np}Gildas!
{np}Ah...{hero}...?{pp}You are...unharmed. That is well. That is...
{np}Gildas, no!
{np}An...unfitting end to my research...
{np}Wait, Nybeth!
{np}She says she wants to return to Golyat and will not listen to reason...the wretched girl.
{np}It is only a half-day's journey, Your Grace. Why not indulge her?
{np}Indulge her? When our ranks are filled with men and women eager to see home and hearth again?{pp}Besides...we need Catiua here if we're to keep {hero} close.
{np}I understand. Permit me to speak with her.
{np}Gladly.

{np}A word, sybil.
Have you seen Catiua?

{np}Catiua?
...I have not. Not since the noon bread, in truth.
{np}I see. On your way.
{np}I hope she has not done anything rash.
{np}{hero}...{pp}I am alone without you.
{np}No. You have always been alone.
{np}Lanselot Tartaros! What are you doing here?
{np}Your mother left this world upon your birth.{pp}And your father followed her only a few months before the war broke out.{pp}Your blood begins and ends with you, Catiua. You are alone, truly.
{np}What are you talking about? I have a brother! Surely you've not forgotten {hero}!
{np}I gather you have realized the abuna was not your father.{pp}Yet you assumed that your "brother" shared your orphaned lineage.{pp}You assumed...wrongly.
{np}Then who am I? Who do you say I am!?
{np}Versalia.{pp}Your true name is Versalia Oberyth.

{np}Versalia Oberyth...
That's not possible.
{np}You are cautious. Good.{pp}House Oberyth gave Valeria her king. You are his daughter.

{np}But it was not Queen Vernotta who bore you into this world.{pp}One of her handmaidens, a girl named Mannaflora, caught the king's eye.{pp}But even as you quickened in the womb, the queen carried the unborn prince.{pp}Wanting no rival for her son, she expelled your mother from the castle before you were born.{pp}Mannaflora died giving birth to you.
{np}Who would believe such a tale?

{np}It was the Bakram regent, Brantyn Morne, who took you in.{pp}He left you in the care of his brother, Abuna Prancet.{pp}Were it not for you and your secret, a man such as Brantyn would never have risen so high or so swift.
{np}Nonsense and lies!
{np}But there is proof: your necklace.
{np}It bears an inscription, written in the old tongue. One with your religious training should have no trouble reading it.

{np}Labon Versalia xan phon, destonia lera phoenan.{pp}To my daughter Versalia, eternal beloved.{pp}A gift from King Dorgalua to celebrate your birth.{pp}{FF 92}The queen made it appear as though you and your mother had been killed.{pp}He went to his grave full expecting to meet you in the beyond.
{np}You must have read that inscription. Nurtured doubts about your origins.{pp}Am I wrong?
{np}What do you want from me?
{np}For you to return with us to Heim.
{np}There, Abuna Prancet can answer any other questions you may have.
{np}This way, Princess Catiua.
{np}Sorry to keep you waiting, Your Grace.

{np}Yes, yes.
Be seated.

{np}The Dark Knights have agreed to an informal meeting. We must convince them that we seek a truce with the Bakram.{pp}Naturally, with the Dark Knights mediating the negotiations.{pp}Ah, it's almost too good to be true.{pp}I needn't tell you I have no intention of forging a truce.{pp}Brantyn must die if we are to realize our ambitions.{pp}Besides, what assurance have we that he would abide by such an agreement?{pp}Too many have died to end this with half measures.
{np}Then we move forward with our plans to retake Rhime.
{np}What? We can't openly defy the Dark Knights!
{np}The prospect unmans you? It would not be the first time you faced them in battle.
{np}They think us weary of fighting, and that shall be their undoing.{pp}Their conceit blinds them. They will not expect us to fight any more than they will expect us to win.
{np}We will seize Sir Lanselot at the parley.{pp}The Dark Knights won't dare move against us while we hold their high champion.
{np}And what of the Bakram forces at Rhime?
{np}Your company will recapture the city.
{np}How are we meant to reach her, much less take her?{pp}While one man or two might approach undetected, an entire company is likely to draw notice.
{np}True, you cannot hope to cross Golborza without alerting them.
{np}Golborza is out, and they will have eyes along the coast.{pp}The Burnham Massif rises to the west, but― You can't think we'll scale mountains to reach them!
{np}Why not? It's the last thing they would expect.
{np}There's no one else I can trust with this.

{np}Dark news, Your Grace.
Coritanae has fallen!

{np}No need for alarm.
All goes as planned.

{np}We witness the death rattle of Balbatos's men.{pp}We drew down our numbers at Coritanae to lure them to one place―the easier to snuff them out.{pp}It aids in our deception of the Dark Knights, as well. They will think us desperate.
{np}Our hero should be capable of dealing with Coritanae as well, no? Good.{pp}Now, we had best be going. There's much to be done.
{np}We move, Your Grace.
{np}Over here! He's on the roof!
{np}Piss and blood.
{np}What? The Walister!?
{np}Vyce! Are you all right?
{np}I can look after myself.

{np}You! After him!
I'll deal with these!

{np}I will avenge my lord. 
For Balbatos!

{np}Warriors of Galgastan! Lay down your arms and surrender!{pp}Your clansmen do not wish to see you continue this fight. Nor do they wish to see you dead!{pp}Don't throw away your lives. Join us in rebuilding this land!
{np}Empty words! A Galgastani does not fool so easily!

{np}We are too few.
We cannot hold them.{pp}I will go to my grave with a glad heart if I can take but one more Walister with me!
{np}You cannot hope to win. At least show the good sense to concede.
{np}What am I meant to concede?
{np}The battle is decided. Shedding more blood will change nothing.{pp}We are all Valerian here. It is Lodis who gains when we kill each other.

{np}What do you know of it, Walister fool? We do not forget the injustices done to our fathers!{pp}In the last great war, the Walister were quick to side with Dorgalua and move against my people.{pp}We were imprisoned without cause. Left to rot and die.{pp}The weight of their suffering and anguish is on your heads!{pp}A debt that you and your seed will repay in blood!
{np}My words fall on deaf ears.
{np}Forgive me, Balbatos.

{np}No time to rest!
Coritanae will be ours again!
{np}We may be all that's left of Galgastan. But we'll fight to the last.{pp}Look well, boy. This is how men of honor meet death!

{np}Tell me! Why do you follow the duke, {hero} of Golyat?{pp}He lays the blame for Balmamusa at your door, brings disgrace upon your name. Your own kinsmen revile you as a traitor.{pp}But like a beaten cur, you return for more. How do you live with yourself?

{np}I have always done what I thought best. Who can do more?{pp}When the duke ordered Balmamusa put to the torch, I refused. They deserved better than to be used as pieces in his game.{pp}But the Wheel has turned. Only a fool would press a dagger to the duke's throat with a Bakram knife at his back!

{np}I see the principle that guides you, such as it is.{pp}When you accept the choices offered you by another, you do their bidding.{pp}How can a creature unable to make his own choices know which course is best?{pp}But you do not trouble yourself with wondering what's best for kin or for country. You choose only what's best for yourself!{pp}You are driven by survival. It is cowardice guides your hand!
{np}Enough!
{np}Do you think we've forgotten what you've done? If this is the fruit of principles, what good are they?

{np}Fool! Good and evil are matters decided by history.{pp}A hundred years hence, the bards will sing of our noble struggle against Walister oppression.{pp}To make it so, we need only win. It is the victor who pens the tale!
{np}Then Balbatos and all his works are surely evil, for he has lost! Your deaths are only the epilogue.

{np}True enough. We have lost.{pp}But you know the duke for the monster he is. You can shut your eyes, but he won't go away.{pp}And when he is defeated, when he stands revealed, you are the one they will vilify!{pp}You knew him for a tyrant and did nothing. When they sing of the Walister, let them sing of that!
{np}Bested by a mere pawn. The fates are cruel.
{np}Defeat is a bitter draught...
{np}Vyce, are you there? If you can hear me, answer!
{np}Did you think to buy my loyalty by saving my life?
{np}I only wanted to help.
{np}Do me no favors!{pp}I swear to you, someday you'll regret saving me.
{np}We can ill afford casualties before we've even reached Rhime. Be careful!
{np}Steady on. The real battle lies ahead!
{np}You don't understand what you're doing!
{np}I assure you I do. You'll make a most valuable hostage.{pp}Though in truth we had hoped to capture Lanselot, not his second.
{np}Fool! Hadn't you guessed the true purpose of this meeting?{pp}We were prepared to hand these isles over to your Resistance.{pp}You've thrown away your one chance at greatness!
{np}Silence! I cannot bear such arrogance.{pp}Grown tired of Brantyn, have you? Thought to find a new puppet?{pp}We need no borrowed steel to crush the Bakram!

{np}Leonar.
The time is ripe.
{np}Send word to {hero}. Tell him everything is in place.{pp}The enemy must not hear of this―not one whisper!
{np}Understood, m'lord.
{np}Your armies already march? When? How?
{np}Ha! You can't truly think we'd tell you.
{np}You'll pay dearly for this!
{np}Were I you, I should be more worried about myself.{pp}You're safe enough...for a time. After all, you're no good to us dead.{pp}Until Rhime falls, you will remain here as our...guest.
{np}Bakram marauders, hear me.{pp}You trespass on Walister soil. You defile the noble city of Rhime with your presence.{pp}Throw down your weapons and quit this place.
{np}How's this? Where did they come from?
{np}What matter? The Dark Knights will make quick work of them.
{np}You! My brother's death is on your head!
{np}Dame Ozma, we've just received word. They hold Sir Balxephon hostage.
{np}What!? They force our hand.
{np}Damn them! We must withdraw!
{np}Do not look to Lodis to save you.{pp}See how they leave you in your hour of need?
{np}He's right. The Dark Knights do not come. We're alone.
{np}Faith, mage! I pull a hair for Lodis. We can handle this rabble.{pp}Past time we put these Walister in their place. Come on, then!
{np}So much for reasoning with them.
{np}Rhime is ours again!
{np}My lord, I've just come from Rhime. We've retaken the city.
{np}Well done.{pp}Your Grace, I'll send word to our armies at Almorica. Have them begin their march for Phidoch.
{np}Yes, with all haste. We cannot afford them a moment's reprieve.
{np}Sir Balxephon! Thank the Star you're unharmed!
{np}With me! Now!
{np}It's shut tight, sir!
{np}To the side!
{np}Gone! Hells!
{np}Wait...the duke!
{np}Who...holds the power now, Your Grace?
{np}What madness has taken you, Vyce!? You've your blade to the wrong throat, friend!
{np}Leonar! Thank the Father!
{np}Feh. I was hoping you'd keep away.
{np}Cease this at once, Vyce! Why turn on your staunchest ally, your liege?
{np}Quiet, traitor! You...You yourself... Ungk!
{np}Vyce! You're wounded.{pp}Throw down your sword, I'll bind your wounds myself. End this, Vyce.
{np}And be discarded like so much refuse? I know what becomes of those who've outlived their usefulness.
{np}Please! A pardon, I'll issue a pardon! Just spare my life!
{np}Your braying's loud in my ears, old man.
{np}Aaugh!
{np}Ca...tiua...
{np}...He's gone.
{np}No... By the Great Father, no!
{np}Can we truly take Phidoch Castle?
{np}Can we afford to doubt? The die has already been cast.
{np}Perhaps we might hold out against the Bakram host...but against the Dark Knights?
{np}How can we continue on this course without His Grace's guiding hand? We cannot.
{np}You would suggest some peaceful resolution to this? Now!?
{np}He's right. We should attack now, strike before they've time to shore up their defenses.
{np}Time... We have no time. Certainly not for fighting amongst ourselves.
{np}Recall what the duke struggled for! Recall {pal 16}his{palreset} dream!{pp}Do not tell me you have forgotten.

{np}Why have we been fighting all these long months? For the Walister?{pp}Was it to claim this island as our own? From some base greed? No―I say no!{pp}{FF 92}If we were driven by avarice, the Galgastani would have little cause to follow us, or indeed, to do anything but resist us.{pp}For what have we bled, I ask you? Who are our enemies?{pp}Hierophant Balbatos of Galgastan, yes, and Brantyn Morne of the Bakram, and the Dark Knights!{pp}It is these men who have forced our people to sacrifice so much, who have tortured and trampled the people under well-shod heels!{pp}While they remain standing, true peace will find no purchase on these isles.{pp}{FF 92}We must remember, friends, that this is why we fight. To bury them!{pp}Even should it mean my death, I go willingly in the knowledge that I gave every ounce of flesh, every dram of blood to this end.{pp}We have the right in this conflict―justice is on our side―and so are we compelled to action!
{np}Yes, you're right. For the people if not for ourselves.
{np}And for His Grace's memory. We must carry on his struggle!
{np}Sir Leonar! What would you have us do?
{np}Lay siege to Phidoch Castle! Tear her down brick by brick!

{np}Phidoch's walls are stout, but a castle is only as strong as its garrison. The Bakram within stir no fear in me.{pp}{FF 92}The problem is the Dark Knights. If the knights were to ride in force, we would crumble before them.{pp}Therefore, I propose a two-pronged attack to divide their strength.{pp}{FF 92}I will lead one division, and {hero} the other.{pp}Are we agreed?
{np}One of us from the south, the other from the west. I will leave that choice to you.
{np}Stand proud, warriors of Bakram! Our enemy may not wield torches and scythes, but they are a mob!{pp}Focus your attacks on their commander, and they will wither before us! To battle!
{np}Just a little longer before the Loslorien host arrives to relieve us! Hold, for the glory of Bakram, hold!
{np}What takes them so long? Surely Loslorien has not abandoned us!
{np}I don't see any Dark Knights riding from the castle. The rift between the two forces must be wide indeed.
{np}Hold the line...! Hold...
{np}{hero} of Golyat, is it? Impressive to lead the great Walister armies at such a tender age.{pp}And yet here, the record of your conquests comes to an end!
{np}Pity those foolish enough to follow you, boy. Today they will learn the folly of a frontal assault!{pp}It will be too late to beg for your lives once the Dark Knights arrive!
{np}Where could the Dark Knights be? Surely they've not forsaken us!
{np}If we have failed...then...there is no stopping them.
{np}The front line is broken! Phidoch will fall.
{np}And with me sitting the throne. A disgrace!
{np}We must salvage what we can, my lord. Depart at once. Leave the castle's defense to us.
{np}You expect me to desert my post?
{np}The high champion is afield without so much as an honor guard!{pp}I am asking you to protect him!
{np}Of course. We must see to Lanselot.{pp}And there is the matter of the girl besides!
{np}Ozma, the castle is yours.
{np}I'll take good care of her.
{np}Ozma―watch yourself out there.
{np}And you, my lord.
{np}Not a soul...{pp}Hnn?{FF 92}
{np}Catiua!? What are you doing here?

{np}Come to my rescue?
Such a brave knight.
{np}What? Why!?
{np}Ah. There you are, Catiua.
{np}Lanselot!?
{np}It's dangerous here. We're leaving the castle. Come with me.
{np}My lord, I thought you were on the field.
{np}Glad to see you still live, Ozma.
{np}Sir Balxephon awaits you without.
{np}The hour grows late. Take whoever's left and leave the castle.
{np}Sister!?
{np}Strength, Leonar!
{np}The time for strength...passed. It's in...your hands now.
{np}No!
{np}Leave this one to me. The princess must be kept safe!
{np}You will have ample opportunity to avenge your brother later, Ozma.
{np}I will show...restraint.
{np}We leave at once!
{np}Catiua will never mourn you as I mourned Oz. Think on that as your blood wets these stones!
{np}Wait, no! Catiua!
{np}{hero} of Golyat! You will pay for my brother's death!
{np}Your brother? The commander of the Dark Knights at Boed? You have his look... Twins?
{np}Two parts of one soul. And now half of that soul is gone, thanks to you!
{np}Not that you would understand the pain of losing family.

{np}Am I not right? You didn't stop your sister from leaving.{pp}And at Boed, you learned that your father still lived, yet you do not search for him.{pp}You've even left your own chosen friends to die! What do you know of kinship? Of loyalty?{pp}You may play the savior to all, but you think only of yourself.{pp}Family, friends, these are simply the trappings of custom to you. Your soul touches no one!
{np}No! It was the Dark Knights who took my father―and Vyce!
{np}Don't change the subject, {hero}. Your shifting words cannot undo the truth.
{np}You listen to me―

{np}You play the part of the man who has lost much. You pretend to sadness at their loss, yet do not ride to their aid.{pp}Were you troubled when your sister left? I think not. You didn't even look for her.
{np}You... What have you done to my sister!?

{np}What have we done to her? You think her the victim of some queer sorcery?{pp}An entertaining fancy, perhaps, but Catiua came to us of her own will.{pp}She sought the protection of Lodis―because {pal 16}you{palreset} could not help her.
{np}We must buy time for the high champion and Balxephon to escape the castle!
{np}And so it ends... Forgive me, Oz. I will soon join you in that darkest land.
{np}But I will not go alone!

{np}No... Oz... You are un...avenged...{pp}Glory...
Glory to...Lodis!
{np}Why did she go with them? What could she be thinking?
{np}Phaesta! Are you injured!?
{np}Ha! More grist for the mill! I'll make corpses of you all!
{np}Thank...thank you. It seems I am in your debt.
{np}What of Leonar? Where is he?
{np}Taken, inside the castle. I fear he has not long to live!
{np}Thanks, friend. Ye saved my life.
{np}I am ashamed at my own lack of prowess. Thank you, boy.
{np}H-Hierophant...forgive me!
{np}Sir Leonar! It is good to see you.
{np}So the thinning of the guards was your work!
{np}This marks twice you've saved my life.{pp}You have my thanks.
{np}Oh, him? He's no enemy. He's a captive here.
{np}Sir Hobyrim, this way.
{np}This is―
{np}I know you. {hero}, yes?
{np}You can see him!?
{np}Nay. 'Tis more a feeling than a seeing.{pp}He has the air of a hero to him.
{np}{hero} Pavel, if it please you.
{np}It does. I am Hobyrim... Hobyrim Vandam.
{np}Sir Hobyrim may lack the gift of sight, but he is gifted in other ways. Hobyrim Steelsong, they call him.{pp}It was he who dispatched what guards remained here.
{np}I hear you fight the Dark Knights. Are they your true enemy, then?

{np}{select 1}{FF 88 02}1{FF 88 02}.{FF 88 01} In truth, yes.
2. I am no longer certain.
{np}As I draw breath, the Dark Knights are my foemen.{pp}Had they not come to these islands, had they not lent their swords to the Bakram...{pp}This conflict would not be!
{np}I see. In a manner of speaking.
{np}Let me join your struggle, then.{pp}Should I prove more a burden than a boon, I will depart, bearing you no malice.

{np}{select 1}{FF 88 02}1{FF 88 02}.{FF 88 01} You would be welcome.
2. I cannot accept your offer.
{np}It is a puzzle. That they present the clearest danger, I have no doubt.{pp}Yet I feel they are just a piece in a larger game. It is those who would wield such power who trouble me.
{np}You would be a welcome addition.
{np}Ah, with Sir Leonar's permission. I had promised him my sword.
{np}You have it, and my blessing besides.
{np}You make for Asyton, yes?
{np}Then promise me you'll return in one piece.
{np}I'm sorry. Were circumstances different...
{np}Understood. No matter. I am sure we will meet again.
{np}Then my sword goes to you, Leonar, as discussed. I hope it is no burden?
{np}Hardly. I welcome your aid.
{np}You've a keen nose to find me here...{pp}That man we took...a scout of yours, was it? Bah! Ill luck, that.{pp}Well, plenty of time for remorse after we've carved you into sausages. Look sharp!
{np}Xaebos... The assault on Almorica...was not to be.
{np}Yeeearrrgh! Spare me!
{np}Waugh!
{np}You with this quailing excuse for a soldier?
{np}P-Please! Forgiveness! I-I've no quarrel with the Resistance!
{np}H-He's no man! He's a demon!{pp}Thought he couldn't see, we did. Until he left two of me men with stumps for heads!
{np}I'm too young to die here! We...We was just takin' orders!
{np}Leave.
{np}Oh, thank you! Thank you, sir! I'll not forget this! Not for as long as I live!
{np}I said leave!
{np}What's this? Kindness wears armor.
{np}Ah, it does indeed! The young hero of the Resistance, hmm?{pp}I am Hobyrim... Hobyrim Vandam.
{np}Why are you here?
{np}Heard there was a fight going on, 'tween your lot and the Dark Knights.{pp}Thought I might join in.
{np}You've some score to settle with the Dark Knights?
{np}Aye, you might say that.
{np}What if I told you it was they who stole the light from me?
{np}I may not be able to see, but my sword is truer than most.
{np}You've my thanks, then, and my sword.
{np}On that matter, we have a messenger here from the duke.
{np}Let us hear him, then.
{np}The Resistance messenger may enter.
{np}Such a grave assemblage of knights...with the blood on their armor to prove it.
{np}Insolence!
{np}Breathe easy, old man. You'll suffer a bout of the yellow bile.{pp}Besides, it's we who've been wronged here. Oath-breaking is a foul business.
{np}So the duke is piqued. What would you have us do?
{np}Don't worry, I won't ask you to go prostrating yourselves in apology.{pp}We would know the lie of your hearts, that's all.
{np}What if I told you our hearts yearn to see Almorica in flames?

{np}Then I'd shed a tear for the people, whom I would expect to suffer in the conflict to follow.{pp}As I would expect you to lose the favor of every lord who ever sat a throne, in this land or beyond.
{np}Lanselot! I will not suffer any more insults from this churl in our hall!
{np}We maintain our position of neutrality, as before.
{np}Were the Dark Knights that led the van at Rhime equally...neutral?
{np}We are not infallible. There are always those who will act imprudently.
{np}The duke demands proof.
{np}What kind of proof?
{np}I'm glad you asked...
{np}You are mistaken, Sister. I do not do this to abet the duke.
{np}Oh?{pp}Who better to profit from the ousting of Balbatos's men from Coritanae?
{np}Will you two stop this ceaseless bickering? My head rings like a church bell!
{np}Your look, Catiua, could singe the scales off a dragon.
{np}So you will have your way or none at all. Just like a child!

{np}Me? A child?{pp}The days I have spent in the field, fighting for the Walister―only to realize it was not my clan for whom I fought.{pp}This clash between Walister and Galgastani is no more than a power struggle between Balbatos and the duke.{pp}While we who serve suffer!{pp}It's not about who sits the throne. It's about the pain all around us, Sister! That's why I fight.{pp}Do you ever consider your countrymen at all? Or are you too consumed with your own travails to care?
{np}I would ask the same of you!
{np}You've never considered me, not once!
{np}Wait, Sister!
{np}Let her go. She has no ear for you right now.
{np}You can't hide forever, {hero}!
{np}Your reputation precedes you.

{np}A jest!
'Twas a jest!
{np}Hold on now. Wait for me!
{np}For a short time only―I have explained this already!
{np}{hero}, there you are! You must be wary―they've returned!
{np}The headhunters? Then my welcome here is ended.
{np}Nothing could be further from the truth. The folks here love you.{pp}You've the right of this. I know it in my bones.
{np}Thank you.
{np}Look sharp out there!

{np}There you are, {hero}!
I was beginning to think you'd gone to ground a corpse!{pp}My thanks for holding on to that head of yours till I could come claim it.
{np}Not bad at all. I can see how Xapan fell to that blade.

{np}Xapan?
What if I told you it was not I who took his life?
{np}Then I'd call you a poor liar. Not that it much matters.{pp}A man has little need of revenge before a prize so sweet. The price on your head's encouragement enough!
{np}No wonder the Front had their hands full with you lot...

{np}Well, well, well. If it isn't {hero} of Golyat! Fancy meeting you here.{pp}I thought you fled across the waves for sure, headhunters baying at your heels.{pp}The Wheel turns for me today. Your head will make a fine trophy, Vyce be damned!
{np}Branded traitor, pursued by our armies and the Galgastani alike...{pp}You fight well, but what can you possibly hope to achieve at this late hour?
{np}I do not know, in truth. But as long as there is any chance of ending this conflict, I will persevere.

{np}Absurdity! If it's less fighting you want, lay down your sword!{pp}You should have run long before, not challenged us.{pp}It is we who have fought long for peace in this land, while you've run whimpering in your weakness, too craven for a cause!

{np}Laugh all you like, if it please you, but I run from no one.{pp}Your noble cause is little more than lords bickering over land and title―lords who, in their struggle, sow the seeds of further conflict.{pp}If it is true peace you seek, leave the duke. He promises prosperity even as he salts the earth beneath us.{pp}Always an eye for an eye... This war will never end!
{np}Slander and venom, masquerading as wisdom. Let's see if that silvery tongue can turn my blade!

{np}It is you who runs, not I!{pp}You whose words fail to inspire the conviction that comes with truth.{pp}Even should I die here on this field, you will learn I had the right of it one day―may the Father have mercy on you.
{np}Better to die at a traitor's hands than die a traitor myself.
{np}The duke outpaces haste itself.
{np}Sir Hektor and his men are not yet returned, neh?{pp}Send word to the lord commander. Tell him to rally what troops he can.
{np}Hear me. We are not of the Walister Resistance.
{np}What of it? You harbor no more love for us than they.{pp}We defend Galgastani honor to the last!

{np}If you'll not listen to reason, perhaps your men will.{pp}You are defeated, routed by the duke's armies! And yet you persist. Do you not see that this struggle leads nowhere?{pp}Or would you carry on the good hierophant's work and rid the isles of the Walister?
{np}You have us exact! We will fight until the seas run red with Walister blood!

{np}Do all of you share her bloodlust?{pp}If we cross swords this day, the conflict will not end here. Those same swords will be taken up by your children, and ours.{pp}Is that what you want? To me, it sounds a grievous error.
{np}You appeal to the mind, but it is our hearts that move us!{pp}Walister are less than filth―night soil to be cast in the gutter.{pp}We must rid the isles of your kind if there is ever to be peace!

{np}Once you've killed the last of us, who next? The Bakram? Who will follow them?{pp}When the last of your enemies has fallen, what will stop you turning against each other?{pp}Your disparate religions, customs, beliefs―fertile soil for dissent.
{np}I'll not be lectured by this lowly creature!

{np}The Galgastani are not my enemy, nor is any clan. I despise you and your ilk!{pp}With clever tales you pit neighbor against neighbor. And for what? Power?{pp}You poison Valeria and all within her!
{np}Walister filth...

{np}{hero} of Golyat! 
You will answer for Gildora's death!{pp}Clever ploy, feigning to be at odds with the duke. A deception worthy of Balmamusa!
{np}I am not the duke's man. It shames me to think I ever was.{pp}Men like you and the duke think only of your own reward. Do not cast me among you!
{np}How many have you slain to slake your own thirst, eh?{pp}There is blood enough on all our hands, boy!
{np}And soon it will be your blood!
{np}Even now you do the duke's work! Or hadn't you realized?
{np}The duke gains nothing in your death. His head will be the next to fall.

{np}So it is power you seek after all, eh? You wear it well, but I see past the silks and baubles of your "convictions."{pp}You would rule in the duke's place. Hold up the mirror, and you will find him looking back at you.{pp}It is your own ambition you follow!

{np}I pity you. You look on the world and see only avarice and greed.{pp}You are prisoner and gaoler, held hostage by your own base desires.{pp}It is within you to free yourself, if only your pride would let you. Instead you lead your fellows to their doom.
{np}You presume much, boy! What can you know of it?

{np}I know you are beneath contempt. I know you have seduced others as you have seduced yourself.{pp}You fight beneath Balbatos's banner, but it is the carnage of the battlefield that draws you, not loyalty.{pp}You exult in death, and you have not gone wanting!

{np}You dare mock me?
Insolent wretch!{pp}Your deeds give the lie to your words, as they must. Your convictions are a fancy of youth, no more!

{np}Beaten by a boy...
Piss and blood!{pp}Coritanae is yours.
You've bought it at a dear price!
{np}Xaebos! Wait!
{np}Xaebos is fled to Brigantys then?
{np}No doubt about it, my lord.
{np}I have heard the castle stands empty, its lord lost to the war.

{np}In truth no, my lord. As Coritanae sat invested, another force was to lay siege to Brigantys.{pp}The attack at Coritanae was only a feint to lure out the duke's armies.{pp}The Resistance would march unwitting into a trap!{pp}Then the greater force at Brigantys falls upon them to deliver the coup de grace.{pp}Your arrival, however, has left the plan in tatters.
{np}Why tell me all this?

{np}Unlike Xaebos, I know when to bend the knee.
And there's more.
{np}Go on.

{np}There are others in Brigantys Castle―men and women who spoke against Balbatos.{pp}They sought shelter from the hierophant, but Xaebos means to use them as hostages.{pp}The Resistance's distaste for Galgastani hostages makes little difference to him.{pp}Xaebos will dress the ramparts with their corpses before the castle falls, an example to those who would cross him.
{np}The man's mad!
{np}A foul business, my lord. I wanted no part of it.
{np}I thank you for your candor. I will leave for Brigantys at once.
{np}You've a noble heart, my lord.
{np}Noble...
{np}There's more to nobility than blood, my lord.
{np}Then you will return to Golyat?
{np}I shall. Fight on as it please you. I don't give a fig for your war.

{np}{select 1}{FF 88 02}1{FF 88 02}.{FF 88 01} So you're just going to leave me?
2. You're being selfish, Sister.
{np}Then you abandon me.
{np}It was {pal 16}you{palreset} abandoned {pal 16}me{palreset}!
{np}Sister, I would never.
{np}I've always been terrified of being alone...
{np}Avenging our father―is that not why you fight?
{np}Why should I care to avenge him? He is no true father to us.
{np}There is the lie!{pp}You have chosen your war over your sister!{pp}How long until you cast me aside? Until you forget me altogether?
{np}Never, Sister.
{np}Do you ever think of anyone but yourself?
{np}Oh, that's very good, coming from you!
{np}So you do move against Brigantys, {hero} of Golyat!
{np}Perhaps they have cause to name you hero after all. You fit the part.{pp}But Master Nybeth has taught me much of the necromantic arts. Will you endure them so well?
{np}You use souls and corpses for sport! Do you never regret the path you've chosen?

{np}Simple child. Life and death are but two parts of a whole.{pp}Faced with death, a man will do anything to escape it―a soldier is no exception.{pp}This is what battle is: the earnest avoidance of our doom.{pp}I wonder if you can hear them at all. The whispers of the dead. Their cries.{pp}How they yearn to go on fighting! The flames of their vengeance burn bright!
{np}Who are you to use the laments of the dead against them? Why keep them from rest?

{np}How little you understand.{pp}The dead are much like the living, you see. Some there are with pure hearts, gentle and kind.{pp}But there are also ones who hunger to take up the sword once more and ravage the living.{pp}Your war has filled the charnel houses to overflowing. There are legions of dead only too glad to strike at you!
{np}If I must sever their bond with this life a second time, so be it!

{np}Forgive me, Cressida.
I go to walk with Moldova...once more.
{np}The air is chill.{pp}This would make a foul place for battle. Let's on to Brigantys.
{np}That you stand before me can only mean my mother and I are forever parted.
{np}She profaned the dead. I'll not mourn her passing. Yield now, or rejoin her in the Ever-World.
{np}Hektor? What are you doing here?
{np}I've come on word of Master Nybeth. He foresaw these attacks on you and your mother.{pp}He sees much that escapes the ken of lesser men.
{np}But Sir Xaebos would never consent to divide his forces, few as they are.
{np}The high commander turned a blind eye when I made from the castle.{pp}You are the sister of my betrothed, may she rest in peace. I could not sit idle knowing the danger you faced.
{np}Thank you, Hektor.
{np}There is no fiercer guardian of this place than your mother. Her absence is a warning.
{np}This was their work.
{np}Then we have all suffered a dire loss.
{np}Cressida, you should hurry to Brigantys. Let me deal with these dogs!
{np}Rubbish. We fight them together!{pp}They've claimed my sister's life, and now my mother's. I owe them dear!
{np}Please, Cressida! Master Nybeth ordered me to see you returned safe to the castle.{pp}Go. For me, if not for him. After all we've lost, to lose you is more than I could bear!
{np}I'll not go! Not for you, or my father, or anyone!

{np}We are beaten. The high commander would never say as much, but the people of Galgastan are no longer with us.{pp}Master Nybeth is not one to deny hard truths. He sees reality, and so he fears for your safety.{pp}I am a knight. I swore an oath to Galgastan...and your sister. I vowed to stand by them in life, and in death.{pp}I beg you, save yourself. You must understand.{pp}Without you, who would there be to remember Moldova and me as we were?
{np}My sister chose her husband well.
{np}Now my love turns to vengeance, {hero} of Golyat!

{np}I am Hektor Didarro, son of Briam, knight of Galgastan.{pp}I thank the Father for bringing you before me this day, {hero} of Golyat!{pp}On the souls of my destined wife and her mother, I swear you will not live to see another dawn!

{np}You are a ferocious warrior, {hero}. Though you be my foe, I'll not deny you that.{pp}The blood of innocents stains your name, your kinsmen hunt you, and still your blade does not waver.{pp}My father, Briam, had the right of it when he said you would not meet your end here.
{np}I want no praise from a creature of Balbatos.

{np}Fair enough.{pp}Only think not that all of Galgastan's knights gloried in doing as we were bid.{pp}Duty, honor, loyalty...a knight is nothing without these. I could not break the oath I swore to Galgastan.
{np}Then cast down your sword and surrender! It's Xaebos we're after!

{np}No matter how futile my struggle, I'll never surrender.{pp}I will not break the vows I swore to my kingdom and my beloved!{pp}Fate ordained our meeting. To do less than fight to the end is to dishonor those who've fallen!
