{np}You have both your eyes, and yet you see less clearly than do I.{pp}{pal 16}True{palreset} freedom is not granted from above, it is won from below.{pp}And yet the commons look without for a savior, even as they claim sovereignty over their own fate!{pp}They wait and they wait for this savior, never taking that first step toward saving themselves.

{np}Man is not so slothful a creature as that...
They...merely lack our strength.
{np}You are much too pure of heart, holy knight.{pp}The people have no need of dreams. We give them all they need.
{np}And what is that, pray tell?
{np}A strong, unwavering ruler.
{np}You {pal 16}are{palreset} mad.

{np}All men are born with a terrible burden upon their hearts, this insatiable yearning for pleasure.{pp}They do not hesitate to take the lives of others if it will better their own.{pp}And yet, even these base creatures can know guilt. So what do they do? They turn it round.{pp}This is not {pal 16}my{palreset} fault, man says. The world has failed {pal 16}me{palreset}.{pp}Someone must bring order to this chaos!{pp}If the commons want to pursue their pleasure, let them do it in our service, under our rule!
{np}You call this "rule"? This trampling underfoot of all who disagree with you?
{np}We trample no one.{pp}All we do is reach beneath the suppurating flesh of this world and wrench out the source of its ailment.
{np}No. As the body strives to mend itself, so does the heart.{pp}These people you so despise may one day astonish you with their valor!
{np}You have far too much faith in the creature called "man," knight.{pp}People are drawn to power, drawn toward safety. They will betray even their most beloved to obtain it―{pp}Catiua, come!

{np}Catiua!
What are you doing here!?
{np}Allow me to introduce you to your liege, knight.{pp}For this girl is none other than the gift left us by Dynast-King Dorgalua: the Princess Versalia, rightful ruler of Valeria!
{np}As you say, the Bakram are not long for this world.{pp}But, with the princess in our hands, Valeria will beg to serve under Lodis.
{np}Catiua, how... Is this true?

{np}I loved {hero}. As my brother, I loved him.{pp}But he was no brother to me.{pp}He abandoned me.{FF 92}
And now I, him.
{np}Though it pains me to part with the man who took my eye, I see no need to further torment the vanquished.
{np}Wait!
{np}Farewell, knight of Xenobia.

{np}The princess has not been seen since the ceremony.{pp}Not even the officers among the Bakram know her whereabouts, and the regent has lent his spies to the search.{pp}I see no other explanation but that the princess has sided with the Dark Knights.
{np}Then the rift between Brantyn and Tartaros widens.{pp}What word of the Dark Knights?
{np}Most remain garrisoned in Heim.{pp}But many of their commanders, including Tartaros, are conspicuously absent.
{np}Perhaps this is why the Bakram do not move against us.{pp}What could they be scheming?
{np}You asked me to search for the holy knight of Xenobia...
{np}Yes. Have you heard something?
{np}A confession wrung from a scullery maid.{pp}It seems that the holy knight languishes in the dungeon below Heim Castle.
{np}So he lives!
{np}Yes, but under such a guard that not even the Bakram are allowed near.{pp}I was unable to mark him with my own eyes.
{np}Still, you have done much. Go. Rest.
{np}By your leave, Commander.
{np}Catiua...
{np}Commander, should we not move our forces on Heim?
{np}Not as yet.{pp}It would be rash indeed to strike without first knowing the Dark Knights' purpose.

{np}Yes, but the more time that passes before we strike, the weaker we become.{pp}Have you forgotten the way the men speak of the princess?{pp}Soldiers in your own ranks weep aloud at the thought of lifting a sword against Dorgalua's blood!

{np}I know. I know.
All the more reason to not act in haste!
{np}A report, sir!
{np}What is it?
{np}The soldiers at Brigantys have taken hostages and holed up inside the castle!
{np}What are their demands?
{np}Our surrender to the Bakram, sir!
{np}After all the fighting we've been through? Not bloody likely!
{np}So the Order of Philaha joins the fray...{pp}Their followers among the soldiers were many, were they not?
{np}Aye. And their influence has only grown since the princess's appearance.

{np}Not a situation we are like to change.{pp}My sis―the princess's arrival was, for many, the advent of a savior.{pp}Add to this the fact that the late Dynast-King was a fervent follower of Philaha.{pp}How natural for these new converts to rekindle his cry for accord and seek to abandon the fight.
{np}I see no other choice but to meet with these followers of Philaha and speak with them.
{np}Out of the question! It's too dangerous, Commander.
{np}Not if I go alone and unarmed. They will hear me out.
{np}I have looked forward to our meeting, {hero} of Golyat!{pp}You will pay for your crimes against Galgastan with your life!
{np}The bastard's...killed me.
{np}Not a step farther! State your business. Only the faithful are permitted within!
{np}Don't you recognize me? I've come for an audience with your high priest.
{np}I don't much care for your tone!

{np}Steady there!
That's {hero} of Golyat you're talking to.

{np}I am unarmed.
I mean no ill will.
{np}I'll be the judge of that. How do I know you don't have half a dozen soldiers with you?

{np}Leave off.
Sir {hero} isn't the sort to lie to us.
{np}I knew you were always {pal 16}their{palreset} man!
{np}A grave insult.
{np}Sheath your swords.
{np}You too.
{np}I am Olivya, a sybil of the order here.{pp}You wish to meet with our leader, Abuna Prancet? Come this way.

{np}What did you say?
Abuna Prancet?
{np}Yes, your father is here.
{np}I don't understand.

{np}Please, we must hurry.
There isn't much time.
{np}The Great Father Philaha calls him to his side. I'm sorry, {hero}.
{np}When we discovered him in the Corpsevale near Heim, he lacked even the strength to stand.
{np}What place is this "vale"?
{np}It is a small cavern where those afflicted with incurable disease or plague are kept.
{np}Plague...
{np}We did all we could to save him, but his condition only worsens.
{np}The Dark Knights had a hand in this, didn't they.
{np}He was tortured, yes, and made to quaff a vile draught meant to loosen the lips...and the mind.

{np}What? You think this a game!?

{np}I leave this in your hands.

{np}We leave now, Catiua.
{np}I was waiting for you, boy!

{np}A fool? Your friends did not call me so as they died.
{np}And brazen besides!{pp}Allow me to show you something.
{np}Know what this is?{pp}Of course you do not. This marvelous weapon is called a "fusil," and it's far more powerful than any sorcery!
{np}Fie! Worthless, bedeviled contraption!
{np}You! Get him out of here.
{np}As I was saying, contraptions are well and good, but a true knight fights with a sword!{pp}Excepting those who fight with hammers...such as myself!
{np}Ready yourself, {hero} of Golyat! I intend to end you {pal 16}and{palreset} your futile war.

{np}Xenobian!
Why aren't you dead yet?

{np}I've a score to settle with you from Rhime.
{np}Rhime? Ah, yes. You failed to defend her, as I recall, knight.{pp}How are you with your other ladies? You must disappoint {pal 16}them{palreset} as well.
{np}I'd be more worried about my own fortunes in love, were I you.{pp}When I'm finished with you, the ladies will barely know you for a man...let alone a knight.
{np}What have we here? The very Dark Knight who assaulted Rhime, slaughtering innocents by the score!{pp}What have you done with Lanselot? What have you done with my brother!?
{np}The high champion's your brother now, is he?
{np}Quiet, you!
{np}A bird's place is the stewpot, not the battlefield.
{np}I'll peck your eyes out for that!

{np}Mind your taunts.

{np}It's him―I'd know him anywhere!
{np}Something you want to say to me, boy?
{np}{hero}! He's the dog who led the attack on Golyat!
{np}You're certain?
{np}I watched as he butchered our friends...as he slew my father!
{np}The drunk's whelp? If you miss your father, I'll send you to join him!
{np}A courtesy I thought to offer you. You contend with me in this life, and my father in the next!
{np}Now here's a stroke of luck, finding the courtyard in your hands, Barbas.{pp}Of all our knights commander, I always considered you least worthy of the title.

{np}My brother's memory is no fodder for your japes!
{np}I'm surprised. I was convinced you'd forgotten all about your brother.{pp}After all, you seem to have fallen in quite readily with his murderers.

{np}I find myself needing to depart... I suppose I have a good excuse, at least.

{np}You must heed me! To the back chambers at once!

{np}{hero} of Golyat!
May the Chariot favor the better man!

{np}Sister, hear me! You are deceived!{pp}They care nothing about restoring your throne. They seek a relic left by the Dynast-King.{pp}Only one of Dorgalua's blood can help them grasp it... They're using you!

{np}So they serve their own ends. What of it?{pp}It is a fact of life and war that men use others...even as I will use them to defeat you.{pp}At least {pal 16}here{palreset} I know I am needed.

{np}I have no desire for order born of irons and bonds!
{np}Hmph. You remind me of another.{pp}Yes, he said much the same as you! Talk of "freedom."{pp}"People have the right to live out their own lives," was it?{pp}Very well. You may share his fate!
{np}You speak of Lanselot...
{np}Ozma. So you truly have turned your sword against Lodis and Loslorien.
{np}I do not intend to make enemies of either.{pp}I have merely lost faith in you, High Commander.
{np}I always thought well of you, Ozma. Never resting on the laurels you were born to.{pp}A bold spirit, you had. Deep love for your homeland, and a true desire for reform... Pity.

{np}As I respected you, High Commander.{pp}It was through your effort that Lodis rose from its own rot and returned to strength.{pp}But I cannot see a future in the course you and Balxephon take―the way you deceive and rule others with fear.{pp}You bring change, but what follows? Press down upon the people for too long, and you will warp the land and invite destruction.

{np}I'll not deny it.

{np}This is no question of trust, Catiua!{pp}You may well be a princess. You may even end this war. But a darkness grows within you.

{np}{hero}...
You {pal 16}did{palreset} need me.

I was...alone.

{np}An ill-favored day, this is.
{np}This is what comes of looking down at your own feet and ignoring the horizon.

2. I did only what I had to do.

Help us!

{np}I don't want to lose you, Sister.

Why was I born a princess?
{np}Still nothing.

There's no sign of―

{np}Sir.
{np}Come no closer!

I will not part with you again.

I cannot say I'm pleased to see you live.

{np}I am Versalia Oberyth. Withdraw your forces and convey a message to the regent:{pp}The Resistance and I want an end to fighting. We can resolve this with words, not swords.

{np}I make no excuses for what I've done. Put tooth to your words, if you dare!

{np}Ozma of Loslorien? Could it be? What is she doing with those rebels!?{pp}Lord Tartaros remains at His Excellency's side, does he not?{pp}Or...has Lodis betrayed us!?

{np}Glory...to the Knights of Bakram...

{np}Your Eminence!
They've breached the castle gates!
{np}{hero} goes too far!
{np}How stand the knights of Lodis?{pp}You've lost my trust. I hope you've not lost your nerve as well!{pp}Or do you fancy taking my city from me, as a coda to losing the princess in Barnicia!?
{np}Sheathe your anger, Your Excellency. It serves nothing here.

We are two rabbits in the same pot.{pp}Is it the largely uncontested loss of Phidoch and Barnicia that weighs upon your shoulders, or shame at your own inadequacy?{pp}Perhaps you should ride out and {pal 16}face our foes{palreset} if you do not wish to become even more of a laughingstock!
{np}I did not come to talk strategy.{pp}I am come to bid you farewell.

{np}Barbas! What madness has come over you!?

{np}It is only a matter of time before your castle falls! Lay down your sword if you value your life.

{np}I don't know what you're talking about... I don't understand!
{np}Don't let him fluster you, Oelias. Believe in your own strength.
{np}Oh, that won't work, {hero}. She has already seen the truth I speak!{pp}She has communed with her soul and found the answer there, whether she chooses to accept it or not.
{np}Nybeth...Father!{pp}Even if you believe your research is for the good of man, it is anathema, and history will judge you so.

{np}An easy thing to censure me, my son. But can you look upon yourselves and say you are without guilt?{pp}Why have you not thrown down your swords? What you call righteousness is no more than a base struggle for survival.{pp}You close your eyes to the piles of corpses {pal 16}you{palreset} have made, choosing to see only your shining ideals.{pp}Am I any different...perhaps!{pp}For my efforts will bring about true change! You speak of history, but I look to the future!{pp}Yes, many souls may have suffered from my inquiries, but it is a small price to pay.{pp}My sins are for my family, and I will not bow to a senseless oppressor too blind to see the value of my work!

{np}Father, I have no ear for your words or your reasonings. What wisdom can be had from talking to a madman?{pp}I have realized one truth, however. You must be stopped before you can do to another what you have done to me!

{np}You have your father's gift for words, my son! In truth you move my heart!{pp}How unfortunate I cannot restore your body to what it once was...but perhaps that is as it should be, yes?{pp}No more fitting finale to this farce than combat between father and son! Hee! May it entertain you in the afterlife!

{np}You truly believe what you say, Nybeth, don't you. That saddens me.{pp}So many words, grand schemes you build in your mind, when all you build with your hands is corruption.{pp}You would create life, but all you have created is the appearance of life.{pp}You profess love for your family, and yet you have lost them so completely they would rather see you dead.{pp}If your name lingers in history at all, it will be to say that here you faced the Resistance, and here you died.
{np}The young warrior spins a fine tale. But is it truth or fancy?

{np}I can't imagine that it matters whether we defeat you here or not.{pp}It's almost not worth the effort to fight someone so...trivial.{pp}Even to consider its worth is a waste of time, seeing as how you'll likely flee again.
{np}Perhaps you are right. Perhaps these truths I espouse are, in fact, falsehoods―unbeknownst to me, mind you.{pp}But what if I {pal 16}am{palreset} right? Wouldn't you like to know?

{np}Not particularly, no. Words always pale before action, much as dreams fade before achievement.{pp}You have lost your love of family, your thirst for true knowledge, your loyalty to your homeland, and your charity toward your people.{pp}No matter what words we speak here today, you are and will remain a sad, old man who has lost all.
{np}An...unfortunate turn. Though I am not...unprepared.{pp}Demunza, Lord of the Abyss, grant me the destructive fist and merciful heart bound within this ring!{pp}Break your seal!

{np}Ah yes, a much more {pal 16}fitting{palreset} form for one so intimate with death. Hee!{pp}Pure undeath is achievable, you see, provided you use the right tools...{pp}...And you're not too attached to your own humanity!{pp}Something to discuss further next we meet.

{np}I knew you'd flee, Nybeth. And good riddance!{pp}But when you think back on the ideals, the companions, the family you've left behind...{pp}Know that I will have all these things. And you will not.
{np}Hmm... The primordial structures within their bodies fail.{pp}The transformation was...incomplete.
{np}Living Corpse makes undead out of the dead...{pp}While Resurrect merely puts off the true death for a time. Neither is the solution I seek.

{np}I was lucky, perhaps, in the case of the Galgastani knight. Binding soul to flesh is no mean feat!{pp}But true primordial regeneration...that approaches the divine.{pp}I achieve one half of the solution, only to watch the other fall to pieces. As futile as forging swords of glass!
{np}My apologies to you both. You were...failures.{pp}But a necessary sacrifice in the timeless pursuit of eternal, undying youth!
{np}Perhaps I will have to enlist help from another quarter―
{np}Oh? What do we have here?
{np}S-Sir Leonar?
{np}You did me a bad turn at Qadriga―I've been meaning to thank you for that.
{np}I admit I was not expecting company.{pp}{hero} of the Resistance...am I right?{pp}Nice to finally meet you in the flesh, as it were.
{np}I know you. You're Nybeth Obdilord―the corpse-mage from Galgastan.{pp}What have you done to Sir Leonar!?
{np}He and his companion were necessary "materials," shall we say, for my research into immortality. A noble cause, you must agree.
{np}Noble? You profane god's creation and commit sacrilege upon the dead!{pp}Release them, now!

{np}How can I release something that does not exist?{pp}These "men" you see before you are naught more than piles of dirt―or soon would have been, had I left them to decay.{pp}No souls, just animated corpses...{pp}Are you even listening to me? Perhaps this will seize your attention:{pp}Denizens of the abyss! From ink of blackest night, I summon you! Darkness to me!
{np}Now, witness the fruits of my research!

{np}Sir Leonar!
It is I, {hero}!

{np}It's no use, you know. He remembers not one whit of his former life.{pp}How could he, when his soul is gone?{pp}Tell me, do you know why the undead always seem so bent on violence?{pp}It is because death is {pal 16}agony{palreset}...and they despise the living for not suffering as they do.{pp}To the undead mind―such as it is―the only way to ease their pain is to inflict the same upon you!
{np}So Sir Leonar is gone...{pp}Repent swiftly, necromancer, for you join him soon!

{np}What is this place?
What has befallen me?
{np}Sir Leonar!

{np}{hero}...?{pp}Wait...
I remember...death.

{np}What in the hells!?
This body...what demon sorcery is this!?
{np}Xaebos?

{np}Master Nybeth!
What has happened to me? Why am I...

{np}Commander Ronsenbach... You are defiled by my father's sorcery.{pp}Forgive us, Commander. I will not allow this sacrilege to continue!
{np}Sacrilege? My dear child!{pp}Necromancy is a noble art! It is nothing less than the path to salvation of the body and soul.{pp}...The power to overcome death!

{np}Was it salvation you offered my mother and sister in Golyat?{pp}No...you knew it would not be complete.{pp}From the very beginning you knew they would be left in that horrible place betwixt life and death!

{np}I disagree. In this matter, my heart sees {pal 16}truly{palreset} as it has never seen before!{pp}I love Cassandra and Moldova. How could I not try to free them from death's bonds?{pp}No, I must strive to resurrect them, and toward this end, I use my art without hesitation.

{np}So you cling to such dreams, ever lacking the courage to face the truth of your failure.{pp}You talk of freeing your family, but if anyone is captive to death, it is you.{pp}Let me free you from this life, Father, that you may trouble the dead no more!
{np}Nybeth!

{np}Impressive! To come all this way...{pp}I half suspect you are led by the same Dark that shadows my path!{pp}Did you know that I have discovered the purpose for which this temple was constructed?{pp}It was built for people like you! Ah...but I see you are not concerned with such matters.{pp}If you insist on playing the hero come to vanquish me, I shall be happy to act my part.{pp}Denizens of the abyss! From ink of blackest night, I summon you! Darkness to me!
{np}This conflict was foreordained, you know. All is laid out upon the Wheel of Fate, free from the meddling hands of mortals.

{np}Ah...yesss...
So {pal 16}this{palreset} is the Dark!{pp}I am becoming one with you now...
It is... It is ecstasy!{pp}Yes! The Dark has chosen me! The bodies of the unwitting will be my vessels! I am immortal...
{np}Those zombies have that woman surrounded! Wait...what is she doing down here?
{np}There now, go ahead.
{np}Go on, try them!

{np}You, down there! ...What are you?

{np}As you wish, madam.
{np}Denizens of the abyss! From ink of blackest night, I summon you! Darkness, be my hand!
{np}Let us see what these mortals have to offer us by way of entertainment.

{np}There. This is more like it...
{np}The woman from before!

{np}Denizens of the abyss! From ink of blackest night, I summon you! Darkness to me!

{np}I bow to you, surface dweller. You fight well.{pp}If you plan on venturing further, however, know that ambition and curiosity are not your allies.

{np}Ah, wonderful.
I was hoping we'd meet again.{pp}You and that necromancer have even more insatiable appetites for knowledge than I.

But remember.{pp}As long as this palace to the Dark remains, those who dwell upon the surface will venture here to satisfy their desire for power.{pp}And when they come, I will take their bodies as my own, and once again feel warm blood coursing through my veins!{pp}We will meet again.

{np}Children of god, who march upon the field, bereft of blood and flesh!{pp}By the power of the Great Father Philaha, grant your form once again unto the proud Tigers of Burnham!

{np}I cannot believe it has happened, though I feel it with every part of my being!{pp}Great Father Philaha! Praise be to you!
{np}You see? With this relic, and the power of {pal 16}his{palreset} miracle, a body once lost can be reclaimed!{pp}As I predicted, this is the promised land! This is god's great revelation!

{np}A pity the false king's army had to blemish this miracle by witnessing it.{pp}Attack! End their lives! This miracle belongs not to them, but to the Tigers of Burnham!

{np}Lowly beasts that crawl upon the earth, hear my words.{pp}Seek not god's miracle.{pp}These forms you claim by ancient artifice are not life. {np}Don't be deceived...Butcher of Golyat...{pp}The demon pretends...to be divine...
Don't be de...ceived...
{np}Repent, mortals, for your souls are forfeit to heaven!
{np}Angel or no, those are fighting words!

{np}The Butcher of Golyat...
Thought I recognized you.{pp}The Resistance must be desperate to send {hero} himself out relic hunting.
{np}What relics are these?

{np}Do not play coy.
I cannot think you've come all this way simply to see the sights.{pp}Not enough that you have claimed Galgastan for your own. Now you seek to usurp the wisdom of the past besides.{pp}Your appetites are grand, Butcher!

{np}These relics she mentioned―remnants from the age of the dragon lords.{pp}Their knowledge was vast. {np}Ancient grimoires and magicked swords...
{np}Sherri Phoraena? Is that you? I had heard the Resistance slew you in Banhamuba.{pp}The truth is far worse. You are turned traitor against the Bakram!

{np}Hello, Jilessa.
If you've any sense, you'll withdraw now.{pp}The Bakram cannot hope to win with the Dark Knights as their allies.

{np}It may be you're right. But I cannot throw away my homeland as easily as some!{pp}I am a proud Bakram, and will always be so!
{np}Is that pride worth your life?{pp}When you lie dead in an unmarked grave, none will mourn you!

{np}Dame Ozma, is that you?
I can scarce believe my eyes.{pp}Then the rumors are true...
Lodis sides with the Resistance!
{np}I {pal 16}am{palreset} Ozma Glacius, of the Dark Knights Loslorien―no, a knight of Lodis.{pp}But these rumors you speak of, sibyl, are just that: rumors. Not lightly do we forsake our vows.
{np}Then why do you stand among the enemy, poised to strike at us?
{np}It would not do to explain here. Suffice to say, I have my reasons.{pp}My quarrel is not with the Bakram. It is the Dark Knights are my enemy!
{np}As I thought, a common traitor!

{np}I suppose I shall have to grow accustomed to people calling me that.{pp}No matter. It is putting Lodis to rights that concerns me, naught else.{pp}This battle is but one step along the path I must walk.
{np}A convenient tale to tell yourself. Do you find it convinces many?
{np}I do not seek to convince―neither you nor anyone else!{pp}The reasons for my struggle are my own.
{np}Then may your corpse grow cold alongside these Resistance pigspawn!
{np}Falfaday... Reymos...
{np}What now..."my lord"?
{np}We have lost some few soldiers, but I will proceed to Lhazan Fortress as planned.{pp}You will remain here and refortify our position. Make no move until Falfaday and I return.
{np}Refortify with what? The girl and her dragon whelps did for most of my men.
{np}I've arranged for reinforcements. They've met with some unexpected delay, that's all.
{np}I'll give a farthing for every one that makes it here alive...
{np}Did you say something, Cielo?
{np}Not a word, my lord.{pp}What about the girl? If she's for the gallows, I might be able to put her to some...use.

{np}Ocionne, was it?
I want you to show us the way to the fortress.
{np}Why should I help you?
{np}The choice is yours. There are other survivors in the fortress, yes?{pp}We could as easily find the fortress ourselves and kill all within.
{np}You are a wretched coward!
{np}What's this?
{np}I thought to find their host here. I see I am not disappointed.{pp}What horror happened in this place?{pp}Or did this village fall into ruin long ago?

{np}So our reinforcements ran afoul of the Resistance.{pp}Cielo, I leave this to you. 
We march for Lhazan.
{np}Begging your pardon, my lord, but I cannot defend against so many with so few!

{np}You let this rabble unman you? Fool.{pp}I release you from the bonds of death.
Come forth and serve your master!
{np}What cruelty is this?
{np}Deal with them, Cielo.
{np}As you say, "my lord."
{np}Let's be off.
{np}I pray these undead fiends know who their master is.
{np}Best leave while you can, eh? Unless you fancy joining our undead army.
{np}What animals are you to raze this village so?
{np}You're not serious, are you? Look about you.{pp}We've only been here a few days. It's a year at least since whatever happened here happened.
{np}If not you, then who did this?

{np}I'm a mercenary, not an historian.{pp}It's not seven weeks since I reached these islands. Always coin to be had where Lodis is on the move, eh?{pp}Only this time, might be I wagered on the wrong side...
{np}The girl you held captive. Did you find her among these ruins?
{np}You've a good eye. A comely one, her. Pity you and I are enemies, else I think we'd make good friends.
{np}I don't keep filth for friends.{pp}These wyrms you've corrupted―they were hers, were they not?
{np}Right you are.{pp}She said she wanted no armies in her village and fought to drive us out single-handedly.{pp}A bloody battle it was, but our master managed to win it in the end.
{np}So there were survivors...
{np}{hero}, there's something I need to tell you.

{np}Do you remember what Briam told you at Brigantys? That I was one of Balbatos's attendants during the blood war.{pp}When we finally learned the location where the rebels had gone into hiding, the task of rooting them out fell to me.{pp}Vasque is the village where they hid.
{np}You did this!?
{np}I did. I took this peaceful village and reduced it to a smoldering ruin...

{np}Do you remember what Gatialo told you at Coritanae? That I was one of Balbatos's attendants during the blood war.{pp}When we finally learned the location where the rebels had gone into hiding, the task of rooting them out fell to me.{pp}Vasque is the village where they hid.

{np}Do you remember what Apollinaire told you at Coritanae? That I was one of Balbatos's attendants during the blood war.{pp}When we finally learned the location where the rebels had gone into hiding, the task of rooting them out fell to me.{pp}Vasque is the village where they hid.
{np}I don't like the look of this.
{np}Don't turn me into anything...unnatural, my lord.
{np}Are these the villagers?{pp}What have they done to them?
{np}What will running accomplish? You wanted it to end like this.

{np}No...
Never this!

{np}Armies do not come cheap. You killed much of mine, so I had to replenish my ranks.{pp}Not to worry.
Their flesh is not long for this world.{pp}I should think it gone already...

{np}Your butchery ends here.
Release her. Now.

{np}You are awash in blood, and yet you call {pal 16}me{palreset} a butcher?{pp}Death means nothing to you, so long as it brings you closer to your goal. Yours is a crude justice.{pp}You still refuse to accept the massacre at Balmamusa for what it truly was.

{np}Him or me, Ocionne?
Whom will you choose?{pp}This Butcher of Golyat who embraces the very Galgastani who burned this village to the ground.{pp}If you would avenge Vasque's dead, start with him.{pp}Or will you let this butcher succor you?

{np}That's no choice at all.
I'll kill the both of you!
{np}Then I will add your life to my collection.

{np}Wyrmcaller!
I must know: are you a survivor from Vasque?

{np}You! I don't believe it!
What are {pal 16}you{palreset} doing here!?

{np}You recognize me...
Then I have my answer.
{np}I put the village to the torch and killed everyone within...including her family.
{np}{hero}, this girl―

{np}I know, Jeunan.
We cannot fight her.{pp}Even if she turns her blade against us, we must do all we can to save her.
{np}Forgive me, {hero}. You should not be haunted by the ghosts of my past.

{np}{hero}, I cannot bare steel against this girl.
{np}No more than I can, Jeunan.{pp}Even if she turns her blade against us, we must do all we can to save her.
{np}Vile wyrmknight of Galgastan! Today I avenge my mother and father!{pp}Make peace with your gods, if any will have you!
{np}You may have forgotten that day, but I will never forget!{pp}Joining the Resistance will not cleanse you of your sins!
{np}My name is Jeunan Avertif. It was my men who attacked and destroyed Vasque.{pp}I have carried the burden of that day ever since. I'm so sorry.

{np}Will your apology bring back the dead? Will it bring back my parents?{pp}If you knew what you did was wrong, why do it?{pp}But it's too late now...
It's too late!

{np}I know no apology can absolve my sins.{pp}But can you give me time to make penance for them?{pp}I fight alongside {hero} to end this war―a war I helped to start.{pp}It seems only fitting that I help to finish it as well.{pp}When the war is over, my life is yours. I swear it!
{np}So you can die with redemption in your heart? Never!
{np}He burned your village. He admits as much.{pp}But it was Balbatos who put him to it.{pp}Rebels had taken refuge in Vasque. They had to be dealt with.
{np}What of it?{pp}Suppose Balbatos did put him to it. Is he no less guilty?
{np}No. But his remorse is sincere.

{np}Mother... Father...
I could not...avenge you.
{np}Another life I could not save...

{np}The temple's secrets...
So close...

Your life is mine now.

As you have sworn to do?

Finish what you meant to say.

2. No. Let's have it.

{np}This is where it all started.{pp}I was here...and all I could do was watch, powerless, as they tore my life apart.{pp}But I'm not so powerless this time!
{np}It's all right. They're tough, but not so tough they won't crack.

{np}Not only do they stand their ground, but we're taking damage.{pp}How could the presence of a force this strong have been overlooked until now?{pp}Perplexing that their commander appears to be a youth―but more perplexing still is their ability...{pp}This could well shift the balance of power between the clans.{pp}Something is exceedingly odd about this...

{np}Looking at it now, it's obvious how unusual this whole thing was.{pp}I mean, seven officers of the Dark Knights, sent to attack a tiny port village?{pp}That's an awful lot of muscle to put toward something like this.{pp}Tartaros understood―he knew that Golyat was key to the Dark Knight's plans.{pp}And now we're here, right in the middle of it.{pp}We have to win.
{np}The Knights Loslorien attacked our town to find my father...no, to find me.{pp}The Wheel of Fortune began to turn for us here.{pp}And now we can change fate... We can save so many from death!

{np}{pal 16}Two{palreset} Ozmas?
What vile sorcery is this?
{np}I am Ozma of House Gladius in truth, but I am not the Ozma you know.{pp}I know everything, Balxephon. I know why you are here―and who you and the high commander truly are.

{np}Go on deceiving your companions, deceiving Lodis if you wish.{pp}But know that all will be revealed in due time.{pp}And when the other me standing there realizes the truth, she will surely turn her blade against you.
{np}A Holy Knight of Xenobia? Could he have followed us here?{pp}No, we would have heard something of this before now, surely!
{np}Dark Knight Lanselot! I did not expect to find you here, but I cannot say I am displeased.{pp}Your folly ends now!
{np}So it {pal 16}is{palreset} you!{pp}Our whisperers and farseers have been asleep at their posts, it seems!

{np}What is this?{pp}The Xenobian knight, a second Ozma... I refuse to believe they are mere conjurings!{pp}Could it be that they have ridden ahead of us upon the Wheel and seen our fated destination?{pp}That {pal 16}would{palreset} account for their knowledge...and strength.
{np}You... Hobyrim! What are you doing here!?
{np}Stopping your schemes, Balxephon!{pp}I will not permit you to claim innocent lives to satisfy base ambition!

{np}What I do, I do for Lodis!{pp}Clearly you fail to understand. Nor do you seem to value the life I gave you!{pp}Very well, I will finish what I started and put you out of your misery. It is the least I can do for my brother!
{np}I struck a devil's bargain with Lodis...

{np}High Commander, forgive me...
Glory to Lodis.
{np}How could I have underestimated them so gravely... I die of shame if not by my wounds!
{np}Feh! Just my luck to die in this backwater!
{np}How is it possible that these {pal 16}nobodies{palreset} have defeated me!?
{np}I underestimated my foe to my sorrow. Forgive me, High Commander, but I must retreat.

{np}I waste my blood on this lot...
Too much remains to be done.
{np}You're...not from this spoke on the Wheel...are you, boy.
{np}Father! Someone comes! They're here! We must flee!
{np}Hmm?
{np}No, I can handle this. You must wait inside.
{np}But, Father!
{np}Trust me, Son. I am in no danger.
{np}Welcome home, {hero}.
{np}You've put on some muscle. You look well. You look like...a man.
{np}All is done as you asked.{pp}My sister is queen of Valeria, and all those who wished Valeria harm have been driven from our shores.
{np}That is good news.
{np}Father, I'm sorry...I...I could not save you.{pp}But I did all you asked, for you. I did all I could.

{np}Then you have done well, {hero}.{pp}But you did not do it for me.
You have your own aspirations now.{pp}Follow them.
They do me proud.
{np}Father, all is done.
{np}You really leaving, {hero}?
{np}If I stay on this island, I'll only be in my sister's way.
{np}In my way? Not at all!
{np}As long as there are people who consider my presence as a count against the queen, I'd best remain absent.
{np}Those blasted nobles sprang up like toadstools after a shower when the war ended.
{np}Besides, I made a promise to Sir Lanselot and Canopus that I would visit them in Xenobia.{pp}But I will return to Valeria and put what I learn abroad to good use.

{np}I understand, {hero}.
I will await your return. As long as it takes, I will wait.
{np}Leave the protection of the queen to me then. I'll guard her with my life.
{np}Well, Vyce. How noble!
{np}Don't jest, Catiua. You know I've always looked out for you.
{np}It's a relief to know you're in good hands. I was never worried.
{np}As well you shouldn't be. I'm more concerned about living up to our parents' expectations.
{np}Go, {hero}. Learn. And bring back lots of stories to tell over our cups.
{np}Aye, that I will. I look forward to telling you much.
{np}So, what's after your coronation, Sister? A wedding, perhaps?
{np}Mmm, yes. Very important for the monarch to have a family. Lends stability to the land.
{np}Stop that, the both of you! I'll keep my own counsel on that matter, thank you very much.
